jobs.title: Sales Manager, SMB - Global Cloud
jobs.description:
About Rippling

Rippling is the first way for businesses to manage all of their HR & IT—payroll, benefits, computers, apps, and more—in one unified workforce platform.

By connecting every business system to one source of truth for employee data, businesses can automate all of the manual work they normally need to do to make employee changes. Take onboarding, for example. With Rippling, you can just click a button and set up a new employees’ payroll, health insurance, work computer, and third-party apps—like Slack, Zoom, and Office 365—all within 90 seconds.

Based in San Francisco, CA, Rippling has raised $1.2B from the world's top investors—including Kleiner Perkins, Founders Fund, Sequoia, Bedrock, and Greenoaks—and was named one of America's best startup employers by Forbes (#12 out of 500).

About the role

As a Global Payroll Sales Manager, you will lead and develop a team of Account Executives responsible for Global Products (EOR, Global Payroll, Global Payroll Contractors) in a fast paced, high growth organization. Your leadership will have a direct impact on the growth of the Global Payroll team, the training and development of your AEs, and be an integral part of defining the Global Payroll playbook. This position will be building the team and processes to support growth in the organization, and will report to our VP Sales, Global Payroll.

What you will do

• Manage, coach, and scale a team of Global Payroll Account Executives
• Build the Global AE playbook and best practices for growth and scale
• Assist your team throughout their strategic sales cycles by deeply understanding customers needs and mapping them to the value of Rippling
• Monitor sales performance: activity, pipelines, monthly forecasts, and closed-deals to ensure quota attainment
• Regularly report on team and individual results through pipeline management and forecasting
• Participate in hiring and interviewing process, as well as training and ramp-up of new team members
• Identify and make recommendations for improvement in the areas of process, efficiency and productivity
• Work cross functionally with other AE teams, Account Managers, marketing, revenue operations, implementation, and other complementary teams

What you will need

• An experienced sales manager with 3-5+ years of experience in tech sales
• A top performer with a consistent track record of exceeding targets as a manager and individual contributor
• Able to accurately forecast team performance, with an ability to deliver concrete and constructive feedback to your team
• Motivated with a desire to learn and have a strong work ethic
• Experience selling Global Payroll, EOR, or HRIS/HCM software (preferred, not required)
• Ability to thrive in a fast paced environment

Additional Information

This role will receive a competitive On-Target Earnings (base salary + sales commission) + benefits + equity. The On-Target Earnings* for US-based employees will be aligned to the range below.

A variety of factors are considered when determining someone’s compensation–including a candidate’s professional background, experience, and location. Final offer amounts may vary from the amounts listed above.

*Commission is not guaranteed

Pay range:
$260,000 USD per year (US) OTE

jobs.title: Industrial Technician - Elko, Nevada
jobs.description:
JOB POSITION:  Industrial Technician

Are you interested in becoming an experienced Overhead Crane Service Technician? Join Konecranes, one of the world’s largest material handling companies. We're seeking skilled individuals with electrical and mechanical expertise, comfortable working at extreme heights. Our service technicians, the heart of our industry, thrive in a safety-first environment. You'll troubleshoot 480 3-phase motors, address crane issues, and collaborate with clients and facility directors to meet service needs across the United States.

Principal Responsibilities:

• Conduct inspections, maintenance, and repairs on electric overhead traveling cranes and hoists at customer locations.
• Provide on-call service as part of a rotation, including after-hours support.
• Troubleshoot electrical, mechanical, structural, and electronic issues on-site.
• Perform post-repair audits to ensure safety features are functional.
• Document findings and recommend corrective actions, including safety notifications to customers.
• Consult with customers on repair and safety issues, offering recommendations for material handling improvement.
• Produce electronic documentation using company tools, obtaining customer signatures.
• Stay updated on industry codes and regulations (OSHA, ANSI, CMAA, HMI).
• Complete service reports and other required documents accurately and promptly.
• Communicate with the Field Operations Manager and Service Coordinator following established practices
• Maintain company-issued equipment, vehicles, and assets in proper working order.
• Operate tools, equipment, and vehicles, reporting deficiencies to the supervisor.
• Follow established safety rules and procedures, including customer guidelines.
• Participate in monthly safety meetings.
• Perform other responsibilities as assigned by the supervisor.

Education: High School Diploma required. Associate degree in Industrial Electrical and/or Mechanical Technology or related field preferred or equivalent vocational/technical training and experience.

Experience: Minimum one (1) year experience involving electrical troubleshooting and mechanical repair. Some electronic experience but not necessary. Prior experience with cranes is a benefit, but not required.

Other Requirements: Must have and maintain a good driving record, including a valid driver's license. Must be willing to work off the ground. Can work varied overtime, as needed by customer, be available for "on call" as part of the service office rotation and be able to travel and work out of town, on occasion.

Must be able to frequently lift to 25 lbs. Must be able to lift up to 50 lbs. on a daily basis. Must be able to lift to 75 lbs. although not on a daily basis. Must be able to lift 100 lbs. on a rare basis. This position requires frequent climbing, balancing, stooping/crouching, and overhead reaching. This position requires occasional pushing, pulling, kneeling, and crawling. This position will be inside approximately 90% of the time and outside approximately 10% of the time. This position will be frequently exposed to heat, cold, noise and heights.

What we offer:

Salary: $22 - $48 an hour - Pay is determined based on skills, geographic location, internal equity, market/data analysis, number of years of prior relevant experience, degrees and/or certifications, technical assessment score, etc.

Company Vehicle: Our Service Technicians get a work truck and a gas card to be used for business purposes. Candidates must pass a Motor Vehicle Record (MVR) check.

Benefits: Medical Plan, Dental, Vision, 401k plan with a match from day one, identity theft protection, accident insurance, travel insurance and so much more!

Vacation: 2 weeks of vacation per year (pro-rated for the first year depending on start date). 5-12 years of service, 3 weeks. 13+ years of service, 4 weeks.

Sick Leave: 5 days of Sick Leave per year. Pro-rated the first year after 90 days of service

Holidays: 10 paid holidays per year

Konecranes moves what matters. Konecranes is a global leader in material handling solutions, serving a broad range of customers across multiple industries. We consistently set the industry benchmark, from everyday improvements to the breakthroughs at moments that matter most, because we know we can always find a safer, more productive and sustainable way. That's why, with 16 000+ professionals in over 50 countries, we are trusted every day to lift, handle and move what the world needs.

jobs.title: Client Solutions Consultant
jobs.location: Singapore, APAC / London, United Kingdom / Boston, United States / San Francisco, United States
jobs.description:
About TEAM LEWIS

TEAM LEWIS is a global marketing agency that has moved from start-up to multi-national in a little over two decades. Its success is due to a combination of factors: it’s ability to read the future and prepare for it; leveraging cutting edge AI; strategic thinkers delivering award winning campaigns; expanding client relationships into new markets or services; and above all, independence from outside investors. The practice, its people and its campaigns have won many awards, including Cannes Lions, PRovoke Media, ICCO, European Excellence, PRCA Digital, Digital Impact, Global Digital Excellence.

At the heart of our community is the TEAM LEWIS Foundation (TLF), a non-profit charitable entity. Since its launch in 2021, it has funded close to 3,000 causes. It is one of the largest employee-directed philanthropies in the world. The TLF promotes a wide variety of social, cultural, and environmental causes that benefit society. It aims to strengthen the bonds between the creative industries, businesses, government, and non-profits. Community charities are championed by employees who, in addition to the financial donation, volunteer their time and skills to maximise grant effectiveness. You can read more here about TEAM LEWIS Foundation.

Purpose of the role

As a Client Solutions Consultant for Orbital, you will identify, develop and close new and different revenue streams beyond our core marketing client base. The goal is to bring Orbital's AI-powered capabilities to new sectors, buyer audiences and use cases. This is a net-new business development mandate. Your success is measured by new logos, new markets and new revenue streams.

Responsibilities

• Identify and pursue new revenue streams for Orbital outside the core marketing ecosystem - new verticals, use cases and buyer audiences beyond existing clients.
• Input into and execute Orbital's commercialisation strategy, tailoring the global playbook to new-market nuances, buying behaviours and regulatory environments.
• Prioritise the highest-value net-new verticals, segments and geographies for entry and expansion.
• Working with the Commercial division and EVP, AI & Growth, develop pricing and packaging models for new markets and buyer types, in partnership with legal and finance.
• Build go-to-market processes and sales playbooks from scratch: prospecting frameworks, pitch decks, demo flows, objection-handling and proposals.
• Partner with Marketing to ensure campaigns and positioning resonate with new buyer audiences.
• Source, qualify and close new accounts, building pipeline through outbound, network activation and inbound - measured on net-new logos and revenue, not existing-account growth.
• Negotiate commercial deals that balance customer value with sustainable terms.
• Represent Orbital at events and conferences to build brand presence and demand among new audiences.
• Leverage your network to accelerate entry into priority markets and strategic net-new accounts.
• Own the net-new revenue number (quarterly and annual) and maintain rigorous pipeline discipline - forecasting, tracking and CRM hygiene.
• Report pipeline health and performance to leadership regularly, flagging and resolving commercial blockers.
• Drive internal awareness and adoption of Orbital, educating teams on its capabilities and supporting colleagues on net-new pitches and strategic opportunities.
• Lead demonstrations and enablement sessions, acting as a primary spokesperson for Orbital and building momentum around AI across the organisation.
• Negotiate partner agreements and build a partner ecosystem that contributes to net-new pipeline and revenue.
• Build thought leadership and a strong professional profile - speaking at events, panels and through LinkedIn, articles and podcasts - raising Orbital's credibility with new audiences.
• Develop relationships with senior industry leaders, partners, analysts and innovation communities relevant to new revenue territories.
• Track competitive dynamics, regulatory trends and procurement behaviours in target markets, and feed insights back to Product, Marketing and leadership.

Qualifications & Experiences

• Background in management/strategy consulting or SaaS sales, with a consultative, solution-selling approach.
• Demonstrable experience opening new markets, sectors or buyer categories. Comfortable being the first commercial face in an unfamiliar vertical.
• Track record of building pipeline from scratch, without an established playbook to inherit.
• Entrepreneurial, self-starter and international mindset. Energised by building your own territory with real autonomy, and a keen interest in AI.
• Curious, high-energy and ambitious, with the flexibility to work across markets and stakeholder types.

This job description is not intended to be an exhaustive list of the responsibilities for this role. Other responsibilities may be added from time to time.

TEAM LEWIS is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to creating and fostering an environment focused on equality, empowerment and respect. We strive to create an inclusive workplace that supports and celebrates our diversity. We continue to invest in our efforts to ensure that TEAM LEWIS is a place where everyone can thrive.

jobs.title: Principal Research Scientist
jobs.description:
The Principal Data Scientist is the senior technical and scientific leader for AbbVie's omnichannel engagement analytics, a data- and analytics-driven engagement optimization program spanning channel mix, content, field representative call planning, and orchestration. Operating within the APEX Enterprise Advanced Analytics and Innovation team, this role sets the multi-year science vision for personalized commercial engagement and is accountable for the technical strategy, methodology, and scientific rigor of the AI/ML and statistical solutions that power it. Reporting to the Associate Director, Data Science, the Principal is a thought partner to commercial and analytics leadership: shaping which problems are worth solving, forming and defending a point of view on how AI creates measurable business value, and partnering with product owners to turn that vision into scalable solutions. The role combines deep, hands-on expertise in applied machine learning, generative AI, causal inference, and experimentation with the consultative skill to align a complex stakeholder ecosystem around the right answer.

Key Responsibilities

• Define the Data Science vision: Own the multi-year Data Science vision and technical roadmap for omnichannel engagement analytics, anticipating where both the business and the field of AI are heading.
• Shape how AI creates business value: identify, size, and prioritize opportunities where AI can drive measurable commercial impact, build the business case, and influence senior leadership decisions on where to invest.
• Lead hands-on with Gen-AI: Personally use AI-assisted development and agentic tools to prototype, test hypotheses, and demonstrate value quickly; build LLM-backed systems using advanced RAG and context engineering, paired with rigorous scientific evaluation frameworks to scale highly reliable omnichannel recommendations.
• Lead the design of predictive and causal models: Develop next-best-action, recommendation, and sequential decision models that inform customer engagement and resource allocation using complex, multi-source data.
• Own measurement science: set the standard for measuring effectiveness, incrementality, and business impact using experimental and quasi-experimental methods, so that AI investments are evaluated rigorously.
• Partner with product owners to shape problems, not just fulfill requirements: co-define business outcomes, scope, and success metrics, and translate them into scalable technical solutions.
• Navigate a complex stakeholder ecosystem: build alignment across brand and marketing leaders, field sales and operations, Medical, Legal and Regulatory (MLR), Compliance, BTS, Digital Lab, and external vendors; reframe requests into well-posed problems and resolve competing priorities.
• Communicate with executive impact: translate complex methods and findings into clear recommendations and compelling narratives for executive and non-technical audiences.
• Productionize at scale: Partner with BTS, Digital Lab, engineering, and platform teams to deploy, monitor, and manage the lifecycle of AI/ML solutions.
• Raise the bar for scientific rigor: establish best practices in model development, code quality, reproducibility, peer review, and responsible AI across the data science community.
• Be a thought leader: stay at the forefront of research and practice in machine learning, generative AI, and causal inference; bring new ideas into the team; provoke rigorous analytical debate; and represent AbbVie's point of view internally and in the broader analytics community.

Supervisory / Management Responsibilities

This role does not carry formal direct report responsibilities but is expected to act as a technical leader and mentor across the broader data science community, raising the bar on scientific rigor and hands-on AI practice. The Principal Data Scientist may lead technical workstreams with external analytics vendors and partners, including oversight of deliverable quality and methodology validation.

Key Competencies

• Scientific Engineering Depth: Deep expertise in machine learning, causal inference, and generative AI, combined with strong engineering discipline in reproducibility, deployment, and enterprise integration.
• AI Fluency and Bias to Action: Uses AI hands-on in daily work to prototype, analyze, and build; critically evaluates AI output; and turns ideas into working solutions quickly.
• Business Judgment and Problem-Framing: Translates ambiguous business challenges into well-scoped problems, connects technical choices to commercial value, and sets long-term technical direction while staying close to delivery.
• Stakeholder Navigation and Executive Influence: Reads organizational dynamics to build alignment across commercial, regulatory, and technology partners, earning trust as a thought partner to win support from senior leaders.
• Thought Leadership: Challenges conventional thinking and sparks meaningful analytical debate with peers and executives.

Education

Bachelor’s Degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Engineering, or another quantitative discipline required; Master’s or PhD in a quantitative field strongly preferred.

Required Experience

• 8+ years of experience in data science, machine learning, or applied science (or 6+ years with a PhD), with a track record of delivering production-quality models that drove measurable business impact.
• Demonstrated experience setting technical direction for a portfolio of AI/ML solutions and influencing decisions of senior business leaders.
• Experience building personalization, recommendation, decision-optimization, or marketing-science solutions, in any industry.
• Deep hands-on expertise in causal inference and experimentation, including A/B testing and quasi-experimental methods, to measure business impact.
• Demonstrated hands-on experience using generative AI and AI-assisted development tools (e.g., LLM APIs, AI coding assistants, agent frameworks) to prototype and deliver solutions, with concrete examples that can be walked through during the interview process.
• Expert proficiency in Python and SQL, with experience in deep learning frameworks (e.g., PyTorch, TensorFlow) and distributed data processing.
• Experience productionizing AI/ML solutions in cloud environments, including deployment, monitoring, and lifecycle management.
• Track record of leading initiatives across complex, cross-functional stakeholder environments and presenting to executive audiences.

Preferred Experience

• Commercial analytics experience in pharmaceutical, biotech, healthcare, or life sciences, including familiarity with data sources such as IQVIA, Symphony Health, APLD, or similar Rx, claims, and engagement data.
• Experience in omnichannel analytics, such as journey analysis, touchpoint measurement, closed-loop measurement, or next-best-action for HCP or patient engagement.
• Experience with advanced ML and optimization methods, including reinforcement learning, multi-armed bandits, transformers, and other approaches for sequential or recommendation use cases.
• Experience building LLM-based and agentic AI systems, including orchestration frameworks, evaluation, and integration through APIs and pipelines.
• Experience with cloud ML platforms and MLOps tools such as Azure ML, Databricks, and MLflow.
• External visibility through conference talks, publications, patents, open-source contributions, or recognized industry thought leadership.
• Experience working in agile product development environments.

jobs.title: Customer Support Specialist
jobs.description:
At Sweep, our mission is to empower businesses to become Forever Companies, creating long-term value while reducing environmental impact and improving social performance.

Climate change is the defining challenge of our time, and we believe businesses can drive meaningful change with the right tools and insights. Sweep’s platform maps climate and ESG data across entire organizations, enabling companies to track, disclose, and take action. By turning sustainability into a competitive advantage, Sweep helps businesses build better, audit-ready programs that contribute to a more sustainable future.

Together, we can make a difference.

Why This Role?

The Customer Support team ensures that our customers have the best possible experience with Sweep— one that is efficient, enjoyable, and supported by reliable, fast, and high-quality responses.

As a Customer Support Specialist, you will support customers throughout their climate and sustainability journey as they use our SaaS solution. You will provide ongoing support through our help center and support channels while building long-term relationships with our users.

You will be part of the Product Department and report to the Customer Support Lead.

This is a hybrid role based in Denver. The successful candidate must be able and willing to work from our Denver office.

What Will You Be Doing?

Your role will be to help customers become successful Sweep users and ensure that the challenges they encounter are managed effectively. You will work closely with teams across Sweep to ensure that customer questions, feedback, and concerns are addressed in a timely and thoughtful manner.

Key Responsibilities

• Monitor and resolve customer issues, including escalations, technical problems, and incidents.
• Reach out to customers to conduct in-depth investigations and develop a clear understanding of their concerns.
• Collaborate closely with Product, Engineering, Delivery, and Customer Success teams to resolve domain-related questions and technical challenges.
• Contribute to the development and maintenance of self-service content, including knowledge base articles, automated workflows, and AI-powered support tools.
• Act as the voice of the customer within Sweep by gathering, analyzing, and communicating customer feedback across the organization.
• Contribute to the continuous improvement of customer satisfaction and NPS/CSAT performance.
• Identify opportunities to improve customer support processes, workflows, and tools.
• Maintain accurate case documentation and ensure customers receive clear updates and timely follow-up.
• Support customers using a B2B SaaS platform, including customers with complex organizational and reporting needs.

What Do You Need to Bring?

Glad you asked. This is who we’re looking for:

Qualifications 🏆

The ideal candidate will bring most of the following:

• 2–3 years of experience in a Customer Support Specialist, Technical Support, Helpdesk, or similar role within a technology company.
• Demonstrated experience supporting customers using a SaaS product.
• Strong written and verbal communication skills in English.
• Ability to connect the dots, investigate issues thoroughly, and identify the underlying cause of customer problems.
• Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple customer cases simultaneously.
• Ability to explain technical or product-related topics clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.
• Experience working cross-functionally with Product, Engineering, Delivery, or Customer Success teams.
• Willingness and ability to work from the Denver office in a hybrid capacity.
• Availability to work 09:00–17:00 Mountain Time.

A Plus ➕

• Experience supporting enterprise accounts or B2B enterprise customers.
• Experience handling complex customer environments, escalations, or incident management.
• Knowledge of CRM, ticketing, and customer success platforms such as Intercom.
• Experience creating help center content, automated workflows, or AI-assisted support resources.
• Experience working in the climate, ESG, sustainability, or carbon accounting space.
• French language skills.

Qualities 🧠

• Empathetic and people-oriented, with a strong focus on creating a positive customer experience.
• Comfortable building relationships with customers and collaborating across teams.
• Quick to respond while prioritizing quality, accuracy, and thoughtful investigation.
• Open to constructive feedback and continuous improvement.
• Enthusiastic, self-motivated, and able to work with a high degree of autonomy.
• Comfortable working in a growing, international SaaS company.

What’s in it for me?

By joining Sweep, you'll be part of a company with a bold vision to change the world. Over the past six years, we've built solid foundations, and now we're ready to think even bigger. Joining us now means playing a real part in that next chapter.

Our hybrid work model, with offices in France (Paris, Montpellier), the United Kingdom (London), and the United States (Denver), gives you the flexibility to balance your personal and professional life while staying genuinely connected with your team.

As a B Corporation, we're dedicated to creating successful businesses that benefit everyone, including society and the planet.

Ready for the most exciting chapter of your career? Come join us on this extraordinary ride!

jobs.title: Chief Engineer
jobs.description:
The Chief Engineer is a working supervisor responsible for leading facilities engineering, operations, maintenance, repair, and technical compliance across CMI’s customer sites in Tennessee.

Work site Locations: Nashville, Knoxville and Memphis

Key Job Functions

• Serve as the senior onsite technical lead and working supervisor for facilities engineering, operations, maintenance, and repair activities; plan, assign, inspect, and document work performed by employees and subcontractors.
• Lead, train, and mentor journeyman, apprentice, HVAC, and general maintenance personnel; verify that personnel possess the training, licenses, and certifications required for the systems and equipment they operate, maintain, adjust, or inspect.
• Operate and maintain electrical, mechanical, HVAC, domestic water and sewer, hydronic, filtration, generator, fire protection, life-safety, lighting, vertical transportation, architectural, structural, security, metering, control, and related building systems within the PWS scope.
• Develop and execute routine, predictive, condition-based, and reactive maintenance strategies that maximize uptime, preserve warranties, prevent premature failure, and comply with manufacturer specifications, the PM Guide, applicable ASHRAE and ASME standards, and other binding requirements.
• Perform and oversee troubleshooting and repairs for boilers, chillers, pumps, motors, controls, sensors, gauges, piping, tubing, expansion tanks, hydronic loops, and Building Automation Systems, including refrigerant recovery and charging when properly certified.
• Maintain occupied spaces and common areas within required temperature, humidity, ventilation, lighting, water-intrusion, odor, access, and safety conditions during occupied hours; promptly report and correct conditions that threaten health, safety, property, or building operations.
• Provide or coordinate 24-hours-a-day, 7-days-a-week emergency response for critical system failures, asset protection, health and safety incidents, and vertical-transportation entrapments; ensure required notifications and response times are met.
• Lead a data-driven continuous commissioning program, optimize equipment schedules and start/stop sequences, identify energy and water waste, support demand-reduction strategies, and pursue no-cost and low-cost utility savings while maintaining tenant comfort.
• Maintain accurate asset, preventive-maintenance, service-call, inspection, testing, repair, subcontractor, permit, certification, and corrective-action records in customer’s National Computerized Maintenance Management System (NCMMS), the official system of record.
• Support development and annual updates of Building Operating Plans, emergency preparedness and response plans, utility demand-reduction plans, facility assessments, and other required technical deliverables.
• Implement quality-control inspections; document deficiencies, root causes, and corrective actions; analyze recurring failures and service-call trends; and support quantitative Acceptable Quality Level performance reporting.
• Inspect mechanical rooms, common areas, equipment, and active work for orderly conditions and compliance with OSHA requirements, NFPA codes, environmental requirements, permits, customer directives, and applicable federal, Tennessee, and local laws; apply the more stringent requirement when standards conflict.
• Coordinate disruptive maintenance with the Contracting Officer’s Representative or designee, support daily operational-status communications and monthly reporting, and immediately escalate major repairs, outages, safety violations, environmental issues, and risks to facility operations.
• Support repair proposals, cost estimates, material and subcontractor coordination, inspections, project execution, and transition activities; maintain common stock and a reliable supplier network while protecting Government data, equipment, keys, badges, and records.

• High school diploma or equivalent required; bachelor’s degree in engineering, facilities management, construction management, or a related field preferred.
• At least 5 years of recent experience leading operations and maintenance for large, complex commercial or Government facilities; experience with a federal portfolio or facilities of approximately 200,000 square feet or greater is strongly preferred.
• EPA Section 608 certification appropriate to assigned refrigerant work and any state or local licenses required for the equipment and work performed.
• Advanced technical credential or equivalent documented experience in stationary engineering, HVAC/refrigeration operations, boiler operations, power engineering, or a related discipline; examples include NAPE, advanced boiler-operator, or IUOE stationary-engineer credentials.
• Demonstrated experience operating, troubleshooting, repairing, and replacing HVAC, boiler, chiller, pump, motor, piping, controls, metering, and Building Automation System components.
• Working knowledge of OSHA, NFPA, ASHRAE, ASME A17, environmental, life-safety, water-quality, and applicable federal, state, and local requirements relevant to facilities operations.
• Ability to read and interpret contract requirements, technical specifications, drawings, schematics, manufacturer instructions, maintenance histories, permits, inspection reports, and operating data.
• Proficiency with computerized maintenance management systems; ability to maintain accurate electronic records and use data to evaluate maintenance performance, equipment condition, service-call trends, and utility performance.
• Ability to respond to emergencies outside normal working hours, satisfy site-access and security requirements, and travel among assigned Tennessee facilities as operational needs require.
• Ability to communicate clearly in English, orally and in writing, with Government representatives, tenants, employees, subcontractors, inspectors, and emergency responders.

COMPETENCIES FOR SUCCESS

• Teamwork
• Results orientation/operational excellence
• Holding self and other accountable
• Operational business thinking

jobs.title: Assistant Facility Project Manager
jobs.description:
The Assistant Facility Project Manager supports the planning, coordination, execution, documentation, and closeout of facilities repair and construction projects across 13 federally owned properties, approximately 150 leased locations, delegated facilities, and future portfolio changes throughout Tennessee. Working under the direction of the Project Manager and in coordination with facilities operations staff, this position helps deliver small projects from initiation through acceptance and provides onsite assistance for larger projects. The role supports safe and compliant execution, cost and schedule control, accurate project records, timely stakeholder communication, and alignment with customer requirements.

Key Job Functions

• Assist the Project Manager with project planning, coordination, execution, and closeout for repair and construction work across owned, leased, and delegated facilities throughout Tennessee.
• Support small projects up to the applicable Simplified Acquisition Threshold, including project conceptualization, site verification, scope development, cost estimating, tenant-funding coordination, kickoff, inspection, acceptance, and closeout.
• Provide onsite project assistance for larger projects led by customer project managers and third-party construction firms, including design reviews, progress meetings, inspections, contractor access, and collection of site-specific information.
• Maintain project schedules, action logs, cost records, risk and issue logs, submittals, meeting minutes, inspection records, photographs, punch lists, and closeout documentation.
• Coordinate with the Project Manager, customer representatives, facility personnel, tenant agencies, contracting personnel, designers, subcontractors, vendors, and other stakeholders to keep work progressing and minimize impacts to occupants and building operations.
• Assist with development and review of scopes of work, independent cost estimates, contractor proposals, project budgets, funding documentation, procurement packages, change documentation, and price-support records.
• Track project costs and commitments, including work funded through the Non-Recurring Work Budget, and help verify that labor, parts, materials, equipment, subcontracted costs, and allowable markups are documented in accordance with contract requirements.
• Monitor field activities for conformance with approved scope, schedule, safety requirements, quality expectations, manufacturer instructions, and applicable federal, state, and local codes; promptly elevate observed deficiencies or risks.
• Coordinate work that may affect tenant operations, occupied space conditions, life-safety systems, access, utilities, vertical transportation, or building systems, and support timely outage and project communications.
• Perform routine site visits and inspections; document progress, quality concerns, schedule variances, safety observations, and corrective actions; and assist with final inspections and punch-list completion.
• Help coordinate building access, badges, keys, parking, escorts, shutdowns, after-hours work, material deliveries, staging areas, and other site logistics required for project execution.
• Enter and maintain accurate project information in required systems, including KAHUA and other applicable acquisition, real estate, maintenance, event-notification, and document-control applications.
• Prepare project status updates and contribute accurate construction, budget, schedule, risk, and closeout information for monthly reports, facility assessments, audits, inspections, and data calls.
• Assist with subcontractor and vendor coordination by tracking qualifications, insurance, submittals, proposals, material lead times, work quality, invoicing support, and completion of corrective actions.
• Support contract transition and continuous-improvement activities by validating project records, organizing turnover documentation, identifying recurring delivery issues, and recommending practical process improvements.

• Education: Bachelor’s degree in construction management, engineering, facilities management, architecture, business administration, or a related field preferred; an associate degree or an equivalent combination of relevant education, training, and experience may be considered.
• Experience: 3 to 5 years of progressively responsible experience supporting commercial facilities, repair, renovation, or construction projects. Experience in federal or other highly regulated facilities, occupied-building projects, government contracting, or multi-site operations is preferred.
• Project coordination: Demonstrated ability to coordinate multiple projects, maintain schedules and action items, organize project documentation, monitor costs, support meetings and inspections, and follow assignments through completion.
• Technical knowledge: Working knowledge of construction and facilities project delivery, including plans and specifications, scopes of work, cost estimates, submittals, requests for information, change documentation, inspections, punch lists, and closeout. General familiarity with commercial building systems is preferred.
• Compliance and safety: Familiarity with OSHA requirements and applicable building, fire, life-safety, accessibility, environmental, and permitting requirements; ability to recognize and promptly report unsafe or noncompliant conditions.
• Financial support: Experience tracking project budgets, estimates, proposals, commitments, invoices, and change documentation, with strong attention to cost accuracy and supporting records.
• Systems and documentation: Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and electronic project-document systems. Experience with scheduling, CMMS, construction-management, or GSA systems, including KAHUA or NCMMS, is preferred.
• Communication: Strong written, verbal, organizational, and interpersonal skills, with the ability to communicate clearly with customers, contractors, facility personnel, and technical stakeholders.
• Credentials: Associate Constructor, Certified Associate in Project Management (CAPM), OSHA 30-hour training, or comparable credential preferred. Project Management Professional (PMP) certification is a plus but not required.
• Other requirements: Ability to obtain and maintain required federal suitability, HSPD-12 credentials, system access, and site access; valid driver’s license; ability to travel throughout Tennessee, visit active work sites, and occasionally support work outside normal business hours.

jobs.title: Facility Project Manager

This position directs the integrated delivery of facilities engineering, operations and maintenance, custodial, administrative support, repair, construction management, and related services. The role is accountable for safe and compliant operations, tenant satisfaction, asset preservation, cost and schedule control, measurable service performance, accurate reporting, and a collaborative partnership with customer stakeholders.

Key Job Functions

• Lead a geographically dispersed team and supplier network, maintains 24/7 emergency-response readiness and continuously improves building reliability, energy performance, data quality, and program value.
• Responsible for contract cost, schedule, quality, technical performance, risk, staffing, subcontractors, suppliers, and required data across the statewide portfolio.
• Direct integrated facilities engineering, operations and maintenance, custodial, administrative support, repairs, and construction management services across geographically dispersed owned, leased, and delegated facilities.
• Establish staffing, supervision, training, succession, and coverage plans that provide qualified personnel, required licenses and certifications, and 24/7 readiness for emergencies, entrapments, life-safety events, critical system failures, and threats to federal property.
• Ensure building systems are operated, maintained, tested, and repaired in accordance with customer requirements, manufacturer requirements, customer policies, OSHA requirements, and applicable federal, state, and local codes, permits, environmental obligations, and industry standards.
• Lead a reliability-centered, data-driven maintenance and continuous commissioning program that maximizes uptime, protects asset life, maintains required space conditions, and improves energy and water performance through operational optimization and demand management.
• Maintain effective programs for life safety, emergency preparedness, workplace safety, water quality, environmental compliance, vertical transportation, building automation and controls, access management, and business continuity; immediately escalate material operational or compliance risks.
• Ensure complete, timely, and accurate use of customer systems and records, including NCMMS and other required acquisition, real estate, project-management, event-notification, and access-control applications; safeguard data integrity and support audits, inspections, and data calls.
• Prepare and deliver contractually required monthly and annual reports, facility assessments, Building Operating Plans, performance dashboards, budget forecasts, utility analyses, project updates, and executive-level briefings with clear risks, trends, recommendations, and corrective actions.
• Oversee small-project delivery from concept, estimating, scope development, and funding coordination through inspection, acceptance, and closeout, and provide onsite coordination and technical support for larger projects.
• Select, manage, and evaluate subcontractors, vendors, and suppliers; verify qualifications and service quality; ensure timely proposals and materials; control costs and markups; and maintain sufficient in-house capability and supplier depth to prevent service delays.
• Build productive relationships with the customer stakeholders and property personnel, tenant agencies, lessors, inspectors, utilities, and third-party contractors; provide timely communications on facility conditions, outages, projects, service disruptions, and tenant concerns.

jobs.title: Fleet Support Administrator
jobs.description:
Are you organized, detail-oriented, and an expert in fleet management and business analysis? As a Fleet Support Administrator at SIXT, you'll play a vital role in ensuring smooth and efficient operations. You'll manage repairs, oversee work orders, and coordinate the day-to-day running of our fleet, ensuring every vehicle is ready for action. Enjoy flexible hours, endless growth opportunities, and a starting salary of $18.50 per hour.

YOUR ROLE AT SIXT

• You will ensure seamless fleet operations by performing daily inventory checks, managing vehicle availability, and coordinating with dealerships and body shops for timely repairs
• You will assist the Fleet Manager in scheduling maintenance and repairs, obtaining estimates, generating purchase orders, and organizing drivers to keep our fleet running smoothly
• You will prepare new vehicles for rental, handling tasks like adding documentation, decals, and tags, and ensuring they are added to our inventory system, ready for our customers
• You will oversee the preparation of vehicles for disposal, completing condition reports, verifying equipment, and coordinating necessary repairs
• You will monitor and track shift activities, including vehicle movements, cleaning schedules, and planning for future fleet demand, ensuring efficient and organized fleet management

YOUR SKILLS MATTER

• Analytical Skills You have strong analytical abilities and can deliver data-driven insights to improve fleet operations and have experience conducting in-depth reporting and analysis
• Organizational Skills You are highly organized, capable of managing fleet inventory, repair schedules, work orders, and documentation, ensuring efficient and smooth fleet operations across all tasks
• Team Collaboration You are a team player who thrives in a fast-paced environment and can handle multiple responsibilities
• Communication Skills You possess excellent communication skills, enabling you to work effectively with all stakeholders and deliver results
• Work Hours & Travel You can work 40 hours per week, including day or evening shifts, and are open to travel (5-10%), some of which may be by airplane
• Uniform & Language You are willing to wear a company uniform and speaking other languages is a plus

WHAT WE OFFER

• Comprehensive Benefits Package Enjoy healthcare coverage (medical, dental, vision), life insurance, critical illness, hospital indemnity, and pet insurance, along with a 401k plan to secure your future
• Paid Time Off & Holidays Benefit from PTO, sick leave, and receive time and a half for working on public holidays
• Bonus Plan Take advantage of a bonus plan based on performance
• Employee Assistance Program Access support whenever needed through our Employee Assistance Program
• Exclusive Employee Rentals Benefit from employee-only rental rates, with family rental options and exclusive discounts for employees
• Uniform & Perks Receive a uniform with weekly dry cleaning, always ensuring a professional appearance

About us:

We are a globally leading mobility service provider with a revenue of €4.3 billion and around 9,000 employees worldwide. Our mobility platform ONE combines our products SIXT rent (car rental), SIXT share (car sharing), SIXT ride (taxi, ride, and chauffeur services), and SIXT+ (car subscription), giving our customers access to our fleet of 360,000 vehicles, the services of 4,000 cooperation partners, and around 5 million drivers worldwide. Together with our franchise partners, we are present in more than 100 countries at 2,000 rental stations. At SIXT, top-tier customer experience and outstanding customer service are our highest priorities. We believe in true entrepreneurship and long-term stability and align our corporate strategy with foresight. Get started with us and apply now!

jobs.title: Operatore esperto addetto al taglio (tempo determinato)
jobs.description:

jobs.title: Sales Trainee
jobs.description:
TRAINING

The Sales Trainee (ST) is a training role.

Upon successful participation in the training program, the ST is eligible to interview for open Account Sales Manager (ASM) roles.

Upon completion of the program and certification, if no ASM or otherwise qualified role is available AND the ST is meeting performance standards, the employee may remain in the ST role up to 12-months OR until an ASM or another qualified role is available (whichever comes first).

Once an ASM or another qualified role is available, the certified ST must interview for that available role.

If promotion to the role of ACCOUNT SALES MANAGER (or other role) does not happen prior to the expiration of the 12-mos completion period, the SALES TRAINEE role will be vacated due to end of assignment unless an exception applies.

For exception, based on continued high performance, no open roles and certification completion, a manager may extend the 12-month completion period an additional 6-months.

AECOM is seeking a Program Controls Senior Scheduler for a critical leadership role supporting complex, multi-project programs. This position is essential to ensuring schedule integrity, alignment, and delivery across programs where precision, foresight, and strong leadership directly impact outcomes.

In this role, you will lead scheduling efforts across medium to large-scale programs, integrating multiple project schedules into a cohesive program framework while managing interdependencies, risks, and resource alignment. You will partner closely with project managers and senior leadership to guide strategic decisions, provide authoritative scheduling oversight, and ensure program objectives are met from early estimating through construction and closeout.

The Program Controls Senior Scheduler will be entrusted with the following critical responsibilities:

• Oversee and execute scheduling-related activities for medium to large-scale programs with meticulous attention to detail.
• Spearhead scheduling efforts across multiple projects within the program, ensuring strict alignment with overall program objectives and seamlessly integrating project schedules into a comprehensive program schedule.
• Identify, develop, and correlate program schedule activities with associated program plans.
• Provide periodic updates and documentation to Program Management.
• Conduct thorough analysis to identify and address interdependencies between projects, proactively mitigating risks and resolving conflicts to maintain program integrity.
• Engage in strategic collaboration with project managers to ensure optimal resource allocation and utilization, critical to program success.
• Maintain close working relationships with senior leadership to define and refine program-level objectives, ensuring alignment with organizational goals.
• Provide authoritative scheduling guidance and rigorous oversight to project controls teams, ensuring effective management of individual project elements and overall program cohesion.
• Implement and continuously monitor risk mitigation strategies, conducting regular evaluations to ensure their effectiveness and adjust as necessary.
• Facilitate clear, concise, and timely communication between project teams and stakeholders, ensuring all parties are fully informed of critical program developments.
• Deliver comprehensive and analytical updates to senior leadership on program progress, challenges, and achievements, providing strategic insights for decision-making.

Minimum Requirements:

• BA/BS plus eight years of relevant experience or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education.

Preferred Requirements:

• Experience with schedule evolution from estimating through design - construction - closeout including changes.
• Experience with schedule management on transportation, water or infrastructure programs.
• Experience on review/development of Time Impact Analysis is preferable.
• Candidate should have experience in reviewing Contractor's Baseline / Update / TIA schedules.
• Candidate should have experience in developing Construction Schedule.

You will partner closely with project managers and senior leadership to guide strategic decisions, provide authoritative scheduling oversight, and ensure program objectives are met from early estimating through construction and closeout.

This is an opportunity for an experienced scheduling professional to influence program-level delivery, mentor high-performing teams, and contribute to the successful execution of transportation programs within a global organization.

The Program Controls Scheduling Manager will be entrusted with the following critical responsibilities:

• Oversee and execute scheduling-related activities for medium to large-scale programs with meticulous attention to detail.
• Spearhead scheduling efforts across multiple projects within the program, ensuring strict alignment with overall program objectives and seamlessly integrating project schedules into a comprehensive program schedule.
• Conduct thorough analysis to identify and address interdependencies between projects, proactively mitigating risks and resolving conflicts to maintain program integrity.
• Engage in strategic collaboration with project managers to ensure optimal resource allocation and utilization, critical to program success.
• Maintain close working relationships with senior leadership to define and refine program-level objectives, ensuring alignment with organizational goals.
• Provide authoritative scheduling guidance and rigorous oversight to project controls teams, ensuring effective management of individual project elements and overall program cohesion.
• Implement and continuously monitor risk mitigation strategies, conducting regular evaluations to ensure their effectiveness and adjust as necessary.
• Facilitate clear, concise, and timely communication between project teams and stakeholders, ensuring all parties are fully informed of critical program developments.
• Deliver comprehensive and analytical updates to senior leadership on program progress, challenges, and achievements, providing strategic insights for decision-making.

Minimum requirements:

• Bachelors degree plus 8 years of related experience, or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education

Preferred Requirements:

• 12 years of related experience or demonstrated equivalency of experience
• Experience with schedule management on transportation, water, and aviation infrastructure programs
• Experience with schedule evolution from estimating through design - construction - closeout including changes

jobs.title: Copy of Productivity Specilaist (Looking For The Next Big Step In Your Career)
jobs.description:
Join a USA Today Top Workplace!

Morris Group, Inc., one of the largest machine tool distribution networks in North America, is a third generation, family owned and operated business that serves manufacturers of precision machined parts in the United States. Our mission is to help manufacturers maintain a competitive advantage in the world economy by improving productivity.

Morris Productivity Specialists comprise the most comprehensive customer service, support, and aftermarket sales organization in the industry. We need your depth of industry experience to bring cutting edge ideas to our customers. Morris is looking for the brightest machinists and programmers to offer the latest products, efficiency-generating solutions, and a level of machine installation customer support that is unmatched by our competitors.

What You Will Contribute:

• Develop strong customer relationships across multiple levels within their organizations: shop floor, programming, engineering, purchasing, and senior management.
• Act as a central knowledge base for machine accessories, workholding, and tooling products to recommend solutions direct to customers and for machine sales planning.
• Analyze customer equipment and processes to recommend products and ideas for improvement to maximize customer efficiency and profitability.
• Partner with capital equipment sales in assigned territory to ensure all customer needs are met from pre-sales to project completion.
• Cultivating a sales territory to generate revenue when not supporting capital machine projects.
• Develop and deliver outstanding customer product demonstrations.
• Attend industry events and supplier training seminars to stay current with new products, processes, and technologies.
• Manage projects collaborating with Morris’ engineering, capital equipment sales, contracts, service, and management teams.
• Possess an in-depth knowledge of the machine tool industry and product lines represented by the company.
• Maintain a high degree of integrity and professionalism that safeguards the trust and confidence of customers and colleagues.

Other Functions:

• Perform related duties as required

The duties listed above are intended only as an illustration of the various types of work that may be performed. The omission of specific statements of duties does not exclude them from the position if the work is similar or a logical assignment to the position.

Qualifications & Competencies:

• Minimum 5 years of machining experience
• Preference for candidates with experience reviewing and processing part prints, fixturing strategies, and tooling selection
• Internally driven with a deep-seated desire to win in a competitive marketplace
• Candidate must bring a strategic approach to all work and creativity for solving challenges
• Ability to work in a fast paced environment and manage multiple priorities
• Ability to excel in a team environment as well as when working independently
• Excellent verbal and written communication skills
• Ability to effectively present products and solutions to customers in one on one and group settings across multiple levels from shop floor to senior management
• Intermediate to advanced knowledge of Microsoft Office suite and other related business programs
• Preference for candidates with lean manufacturing training
• Preference for candidates with public speaking or product presentation experience
• Preference for candidates with project management experience
• Position requires access to reliable transportation, a valid U.S. driver’s license, and a clean driving record
• A current U.S. passport is a plus
• Daily travel throughout the assigned territory with occasional long distance or overnight travel required

What’s in it for You:

We take great pride in our employees and offer a variety of benefits that allow our employees to be successful inside and outside of work:

• Competitive starting salary
• Market competitive comprehensive health benefits including a zero premium medical plan offering, vision, dental, and company paid life insurance
• 3+ Weeks’ Vacation to Start
• 10 Company Paid Holidays
• 401(k) retirement plan with company contribution
• Tuition reimbursement
• Employee appreciation events and perks
• Employee Assistance Program

Mental and Physical Requirements:

The physical demands and characteristics of the work environment described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of the job. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

• Must be highly mobile, able to access all areas of the premises.
• Ability to concentrate and remain focused while prioritizing multiple tasks, responsibilities, and projects.
• Ability to sit for prolonged period of times.
• Able to perform bending, twisting, stooping, reaching, and lifting of moderate to heavyweight material up to 50 lbs. with assistance from equipment or other employees.
• Ability to frequently use hands and arms.
• Vision abilities required by the job include close vision, distance vision, peripheral vision, depth perception and the ability to adjust focus.
• Ability to work responsibly and professionally in dynamic job sites that may involve tight timelines, changing priorities, and interaction with customers and team members.

Certain positions are designated as safety-sensitive due to the nature of the work performed. Employees in these roles may also be expected to:

• Ability to stand, walk, bend, kneel, crouch, climb, and reach for extended periods while servicing equipment.
• Ability to work in tight spaces or awkward positions, including accessing equipment interiors and elevated areas.
• Strong hand–eye coordination and fine motor skills required for precise electrical, mechanical, and diagnostic work.
• Ability to work in industrial environments, with exposure to noise, lubricants, coolants, metal chips, and other manufacturing conditions, while consistently wearing required personal protective equipment (PPE).

Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, protected veteran status or other characteristics protected by law.

jobs.title: Facility Technician
jobs.description:
NBCUniversal is looking for a Facility Technician! In this role, you will be responsible for ensuring the efficient operation, maintenance and repair of building envelopes, systems, equipment, grounds and infrastructure. You will troubleshoot and resolve technical issues, conduct preventative maintenance, respond to service calls, escort vendors on site, and collaborate with contractors to ensure the facility operates efficiently, remains safe and is compliant with all regulations.

What You'll Do:

• Maintain, troubleshoot, and repair mechanical, electrical and plumbing systems, including critical infrastructure, to ensure continuous, efficient, and safe operations
• Monitor building automation systems (BAS) to optimize energy use, systems performance, and maintain comfortable environments for employees and guests
• Address and resolve building system failures in a timely manner to minimize disruptions
• Respond to service requests and emergencies during and after business hours
• Conduct site inspections and meter readings as required
• Complete preventative, corrective and reactive maintenance work orders assigned through the CMMS and mobile platform
• Maintain accurate records of maintenance activity, equipment performance, repair history, and costs in the CMMS
• Work closely with the Asset Management team to ensure assets are tagged and data is accurate in the Master Asset List
• Participate in the development and implementation of standard operating procedures (SOP) and key performance indicators (KPI’s) with Facility Operations and the Asset Management team
• Oversee and support vendor and 3rd party contracted services.
• Schedule and coordinate service calls with internal teams and external vendors
• Partner with NBCU departments to ensure compliance and safety tasks are addressed promptly
• Support emergency preparedness initiatives and attend drills and exercises related to fire, disaster response, and business continuity
• Adhere to OSHA, ADA and other regulatory requirements
• Support Facility Operations and support teams with event set-ups
• Interior & exterior painting and general carpentry tasks as needed
• Attend bid walks and assist with project oversite when required
• Other duties as assigned

Let’s Talk About You:

• Cool Under Pressure – You handle stressful situations with ease and professionalism while juggling multiple stakeholders and competing priorities
• Communicates with ease – You have a way with words; written and verbal
• Tech-savvy – You are an MS Office whiz and can take on new software with ease

What You Have:

• High school diploma or equivalent required;
• 3+ years of experience in building engineering, facilities management or a related field or equivalent
• Understanding of Class A commercial building operations
• Demonstrated proficiency with HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and building automation systems (BAS)
• Knowledge of applicable building codes, safety standards, regulatory requirements, and energy efficiency practices.
• Valid state Class C Driver’s License

What Would Make You Stand Out:

• Associates degree or technical certification in building systems
• Strong troubleshooting and diagnostic skills
• Relevant trade license or certifications (HVAC, electrical, plumbing, low voltage)
• EPA Universal Certification for refrigerants
• Understanding of Class A high rise operations and REG 4

Additional Requirements:

• Required On-Site: This position is required to be performed full-time from an NBCUniversal-designated worksite.
• Ability to work flexible hours and travel as needed

This position is eligible for company sponsored benefits, including medical, dental and vision insurance, 401(k), paid leave, tuition reimbursement, and a variety of other discounts and perks. Learn more about the benefits offered by NBCUniversal by visiting the Benefits page of the Careers website. Salary range: $46.00 - $48.00/hourly

jobs.title: Test Technician
jobs.description:
The Engineering Technician supports semiconductor test operations involving automated test equipment (ATE), wafer probers, handlers, and associated test instrumentation. The ideal candidate has hands-on experience with probers and testers, strong troubleshooting capability, and the ability to collaborate closely with engineering teams to maintain high-quality, high-efficiency test operations. The role also contributes to continuous improvement of test processes and equipment performance.

Business context

Our test operations organization supports new product introduction (NPI), engineering sample evaluation, and production test readiness for advanced Analog, Power, MCU, and EP semiconductor products. This position is key to dependable test cell operation, data generation for engineering analysis, and smooth coordination with suppliers, cross-functional engineering teams, and production support groups.

Key Responsibilities

Test cell operations

• Support small-volume engineering sample and low-volume production programs.

• Set up, dock, and undock ATE systems with probers and handlers according to daily engineering and production needs.

• Perform device-level testing manually using ATE and laboratory test equipment.

Equipment troubleshooting and debug

• Diagnose and troubleshoot handlers, probers, and testers, coordinating with Renesas engineers and vendors as needed to restore operation.

• Debug ATE hardware, including load boards, probe cards, and socketed test fixtures.

• Identify intermittent test board performance issues and escalate to engineering for root-cause resolution.

Data collection

• Collect engineering data using oscilloscopes, network analyzers, multimeters, and basic semiconductor diagnostic tools.

Maintenance, calibration, and compliance

• Perform preventive maintenance (PM) and calibration support for ATE, handlers, probers, and other test equipment.

• Maintain calibration records and PM logs to support ISO-9001 audits.

• Ensure compliance with safety and quality requirements.

Education

• Bachelor / Associate of Science (AS) degree or equivalent in EE, Mechanical or Industrial Engineering

Experience

• 5–10 years of hands-on experience testing on ATE systems.

• Proficiency with wafer probers and handlers, including setup and operation.

• Hardware inventory management system

Technical skills

• Good knowledge of circuit design and troubleshooting.

• Understanding of basic semiconductor test flows and of industry test standards.

• Soldering skills.

• Basic proficiency with MS Word and Excel. Python scripting will be a plus.

Professional skills

• Strong troubleshooting skills and willingness to take on challenging technical tasks.

• Skilled with documentation; excellent verbal and written communication, including with engineers and cross-functional support teams.

• Self-motivated and conscientious; able to complete tasks with minimal supervision.

• Ability to multi-task while maintaining attention to detail.

Preferred Experience

Test Platforms

Advantest 93K, Teradyne Eagle/UFlex, Cohu DiamondX, SPEA DOT800C

Wafer probers

TEL, Accretech

Handlers

Talos, Seiko, JHT, Hontech

The expected annual pay range for this position is 35.00-45.00/hr. This position is also eligible for bonus opportunities. Please note that final offer amount will be dependent on geographic location, applicable experience, and skillset of the candidate.

Renesas is an embedded semiconductor solution provider driven by its Purpose, To Make Our Lives Easier. With a global team of over 21,000 engineers and problem solvers in more than 30 countries, we offer the opportunity to work on world‑leading technology for Automotive, Industrial, Infrastructure, and IoT, shaping a safer, healthier, greener, and smarter future.

At Renesas, TAGIE is our culture, grounded in being Transparent, Agile, Global, Innovative, and Entrepreneurial. It shapes how we work, grow and deliver on our purpose together. This collaborative spirit and mindset drive our semiconductor technology to transform industries and impact millions of lives.

We believe in rewarding our employees with a competitive benefits package alongside their salary. More information will be provided during the hiring process.

Are you ready to join our team and shape the future with us?

jobs.title: Program Controls Cost Manager
jobs.description:
AECOM is seeking a Program Controls – Cost Manager to support complex, high-visibility programs within our East Region. This role sits at the intersection of project controls and program management, supporting initiatives that extend beyond individual projects and carry broader responsibilities tied to government oversight, stakeholder alignment, financial stewardship, and long-term legacy outcomes.

As a Program Controls – Cost Manager, you will provide strategic cost and controls leadership across multi-project programs, ensuring alignment with program objectives while navigating the added complexities of legislation, political considerations, multi-partner KPIs, and cross-organizational collaboration. You will work closely with program leadership, project teams, and stakeholders to drive disciplined execution, transparency, and informed decision-making at the program level.

This is an opportunity for an experienced program controls professional to influence large-scale programs, partner with senior leadership, and help deliver outcomes that matter—while growing your career with a global leader in infrastructure and program management.

The Program Controls Manager is entrusted with the following critical responsibilities:

• Directs and manages program controls related activities for medium-sized programs or specialized defined controls elements of larger programs in support of the Program Manager or Program Controls Director.
• Orchestrates coordination efforts across multiple projects within the program, ensuring strict alignment with overall program objectives.
• Identifies and addresses project interdependencies with utmost diligence, implementing proactive risk mitigation strategies and resolving conflicts.
• Collaborates strategically with project managers to ensure optimal resource allocation and utilization.
• Engages in high-level consultations with senior leadership to define and refine program-level objectives.
• Provides authoritative guidance and rigorous oversight to project controls teams, ensuring meticulous management of individual project elements.
• Conducts thorough monitoring and evaluation of risk mitigation strategies to ensure their efficacy and implement necessary adjustments.
• Facilitates precise and formal communication channels between project teams and stakeholders.
• Delivers comprehensive and regular updates to senior leadership on program progress, challenges, and achievements, maintaining the highest standards of accuracy and professionalism.

Minimum requirements:

• Bachelors degree plus 8 years of related experience or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education.

Preferred Requirements:

• 14 years of related experience or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education.
• Experience with cost management on Transportation, Water and Aviation programs.
• Experience with cost evolution from estimating through design - construction - closeout including changes.

• Sponsorship assistance is not available for this position now or in the future.
• Relocation assistance is not available for this position now or in the future.
• THIS POSTING IS FOR A CURRENT VACANCY, AND AECOM INTENDS TO FILL THIS POSITION BY JANUARY 31, 2027.

jobs.description:
JOB DESCRIPTION SUMMARY

The Maintenance Technician’s job is to keep the plant and equipment running in a safe and efficient manner. Maintains and repairs building and equipment. Carries out responsibilities in accordance with company policies and procedures.

Pay : The starting rate for this role is $23.31 – $43.01(Hourly)

Schedule:  This is a continuous schedule with every other weekend 5 days off

DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

The duties and responsibilities of this position shall consist of, but not be limited to, the following:

Daily work:

• Inspect machines regularly for signs of malfunctions, including visual inspections, listening for irregular noises and conducting scheduled testing as appropriate.
• Perform routine preventative maintenance and service for each piece of equipment, complete daily Work Order documentation and enter into CMMS system.
• Collaboration with site managers to assess ongoing needs and plan preventative maintenance schedules.
• Routine inspection of tools and maintenance equipment.
• Use a variety of power and hand tools to perform job functions.
• Install, assemble and test new machines and equipment.

Troubleshooting:

• Monitor, identify and respond promptly to signs of malfunction in machinery such as changes in performance, temperature fluctuations, sounds, smells or atypical energy usage; perform troubleshooting for production machinery.
• Perform emergency repairs on various types of machinery, including mechanical, electric and hydraulic; identify and replace worn or damaged parts in a timely manner.
• Diagnosis of mechanical and electrical system issues.
• Diagnose and repair mechanical machinery.

General:

• Reading, interpreting, and following instructions and operation manuals.
• Maintain machinery and the adjacent workplace in a state of appropriate cleanliness.

• Assist with inventory control.
• Maintain the shop, mechanical room, and the interior/exterior of the plant.
• Maintain a safe, clean, and organized work area.
• Perform all duties within OSHA and company safety standards; LOTO, wear PPE and maintain safety equipment.
• Ensure safety devices are installed and working properly.
• Follow good manufacturing practices and HACCP training, along with company SOP’s, and SSOP’s.
• Other duties as assigned.

REQUIRED EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

Required Education:  High School Diploma or equivalent.

Required Experience:  Knowledge of the materials, tools, methods, and techniques used in the mechanical, pneumatic, and hydraulic trades. Basic understanding of motors, and controllers, hydraulics and pneumatics, plumbing. Basic understanding of PLC I/O.  Basic understanding of TCP/IP.

Preferred Experience: 2 yr. technical degree and previous experience working in a meat processing facility.

• Robotics maintenance and troubleshooting experience.
• Ammonia refrigeration experience.
• Experience working in food manufacturing environment.
• CMMS experience in at least one CMMS program.
• English/Spanish bilingual.

REQUIRED SKILLS, KNOWLEDGE, AND ABILITIES

• Skill in diagnosing equipment defects and making necessary repairs.
• Must be a team player that is committed to working in a quality environment.
• The ability to work independently with demonstrated ability to prioritize workload effectively.
• The ability to work in a fast paced and dynamic environment.
• Must be an agent for change and receptive to innovative ideas from others.
• The ability to establish and maintain harmonious working relationships with other team members and departments.
• The ability to deal with multiple tasks while using good judgment.
• The ability to perform heavy physical work, exercising up to 50 pounds of strength frequently to lift, carry, push, pull, or otherwise move objects. Work involves stooping, crouching, kneeling, reaching, standing, walking, and grasping.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by a Team Member to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

While performing the duties of this job the Team Member will be required to wear the appropriate Personal Protective Equipment (i.e beard/hairnet, ear plugs, frock, boots, etc), stand for extended periods of time, and use hands/arms to push, pull, reach and occasionally lift above head.  The Team Member must occasionally lift, push, pull up to 25 pounds and 50 pounds infrequently. Team Members are requested to visually inspect equipment and/or product.

WORK ENVIRONMENT

The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those a Team Member encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. The work environment is a plant setting with wet/slippery floors, varying degrees of temperatures with an average temperature of 40 degrees in the production area.  Team Members will be exposed to raw and/or cooked meat products and moving equipment and will be required to follow all Food Safety Quality requirements.

The starting rate for this role is $36.00 – $43.01(Hourly). Actual salaries will vary based on several factors, including but not limited to external market data, internal equity, location, and candidate skill set and experience. New York City, NY - Fifth Avenue

At Rothy’s, we believe there’s a better way to do business—one that puts the planet and its people first. That’s why we’ve transformed millions of plastic bottles into stylish, sustainable shoes and bags, creating wardrobe staples that look just as good as they feel.

In our retail stores, clienteling, and genuine connection are at the heart of everything we do. We take pride in building lasting relationships with our customers—getting to know their style, anticipating their needs, and creating personalized experiences that make them feel truly seen and supported. Whether it’s helping someone find their perfect fit or sharing the story behind our sustainable designs, every interaction is an opportunity to deepen that connection.

As we grow, we’re cultivating not just a workplace, but a community. It’s a place where careers can grow, ideas are shared, and people feel a true sense of belonging. Every day brings new opportunities to learn, lead, and make an impact—together, as part of a welcoming, inclusive team that celebrates each other’s contributions.
