We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, protected veteran status, or disability status. The Operations Supervisor will provide a high level of leadership to ensure customer, team member, and vendor satisfaction. The Operations Supervisor does this by leading a culture of continuous improvement to achieve plant goals in their assigned area. The Operations Supervisor is also responsible for training, developing, and coaching employee has to meet goals and objectives. jobs.title: Staff Software Engineer – Data
jobs.description:
Why Sony Interactive Entertainment?

Sony Interactive Entertainment isn’t just the Best Place to Play — it’s also the Best Place to Work. Sony Interactive Entertainment (SIE) is the company behind the PlayStation brand. As a subsidiary of Sony Group Corporation, we’re part of a proud legacy of innovation and excellence. SIE is a dynamic technology company, delivering cutting-edge hardware and network services to more than 100 million people and an entertainment leader, home to some of the most beloved and recognizable intellectual properties (IP) in the world. Our role at SIE is to create and nurture the experiences under the PlayStation brand, a name synonymous with entertainment excellence and creativity.

Staff Software Engineer – Data

Do you want to join a team of talented engineers building the next generation of real-time data platforms that power analytics and data-driven experiences across PlayStation? As part of our Data Platform team, you will play a key technical leadership role in designing and evolving the Real-Time Analytics Platform (RTAP), enabling high-throughput, low-latency analytics and stream processing at PlayStation scale.

The Software Engineers within our Platform Engineering Group design, build, document, and operate large-scale distributed data platforms that support real-time and near real-time analytics across PlayStation. You will solve complex distributed systems challenges, evolve our streaming and analytics architecture, integrate AI-powered platform capabilities, and improve scalability, reliability, performance, and developer productivity.

We’re looking for someone who is passionate about distributed systems, real-time analytics, and building scalable data platforms. You will work closely with Engineering, Product, Infrastructure, Security, and Data Engineering teams to shape technical strategy, influence architecture across organizations, mentor engineers, and help drive the long-term evolution of PlayStation’s data platform.

Responsibilities

·      Design, build, and operate large-scale distributed data systems that power real-time and near real-time analytics,, and data-driven applications across PlayStation.

·      Lead the architecture and evolution of RTAP’s stream processing and analytics platforms, improving scalability, reliability, performance, and developer productivity.

·      Own critical platform capabilities end-to-end from architecture and implementation through production operations, performance optimization, reliability, and lifecycle management.

·      Build and optimize distributed data services using technologies such as Apache Flink, Spark Structured Streaming, ClickHouse, and Apache Druid to support high-throughput, low-latency workloads.

·      Partner with Data Engineering teams to integrate batch and streaming workloads using modern lakehouse architectures and build interoperable, scalable data platforms.

·      Build AI-powered capabilities to automate engineering workflows, improve data quality, simplify platform operations, accelerate troubleshooting, and enhance developer productivity.

·      Establish technical standards and engineering best practices for distributed systems, stream processing, data modeling, query optimization and platform reliability.

·      Mentor engineers across the organization by reviewing architecture, designs, and code while raising the technical bar through coaching and technical leadership.

·      Partner with Product, Infrastructure, Security, and Platform Engineering teams to define long-term technical strategy and deliver scalable platform capabilities aligned with business priorities.

·      Investigate and resolve complex production challenges involving high-throughput, low-latency distributed systems, ensuring high availability and operational excellence.

·  Participate in the team's production support and on-call rotation, leading incident response, conducting root-cause analysis, and implementing reliability improvements that strengthen the platform over time

·      Evaluate emerging technologies and distributed data platforms, recommending investments that improve scalability, reliability, developer productivity, and cost efficiency.

Requirements

·      Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.

·      8+ years of experience designing and building large-scale distributed systems, with expertise in real-time data processing, analytics, or data platform engineering.

·      Strong proficiency in Python, with experience building production-grade distributed systems and data processing applications. Experience with Scala is beneficial for supporting and evolving existing platform components.

·      Hands-on expertise designing and operating large-scale stream processing applications using Apache Flink, Apache Spark Structured Streaming, or equivalent distributed streaming technologies.

·      Production experience designing, operating, and optimizing distributed analytics platforms using ClickHouse, Apache Druid, or equivalent high-performance OLAP/analytics databases, including query optimization, data modeling, and performance tuning at scale.

·      Experience building and consuming event-driven data pipelines using AWS MSK, Apache Kafka, or equivalent messaging platforms, with a focus on developing reliable, scalable data processing applications.

·      Experience applying AI/ML techniques and modern AI tooling to automate engineering workflows, improve data pipelines, simplify platform operations, and enhance developer productivity.

·      Strong systems design skills with the ability to evaluate architectural trade-offs across scalability, latency, throughput, consistency, reliability, and cost.

·      Demonstrated technical leadership through architecture ownership, mentoring engineers, and influencing technical decisions across multiple teams.

Nice to Have

·      Experience with Databricks, Apache Iceberg, or modern lakehouse architectures, with the ability to design and integrate batch and streaming workloads into scalable, production-grade data platforms.

·      Experience building or operating multi-tenant, self-service data platforms supporting multiple engineering organizations.

·      Experience collaborating with globally distributed engineering teams across multiple organizations and time zones to deliver shared platform capabilities and drive technical alignment.

Your First 90 Days

30 Days: Develop a strong understanding of the platform’s architecture, capabilities, engineering practices, and roadmap.Begin contributing to architecture discussions, feature development, design reviews, and production support.Build relationships within the team as well as across  the Data Platform organization.

60 Days: Take technical ownership of a major platform capability or architectural area.
Identify opportunities to improve scalability, performance, reliability, or developer productivity.Collaborate with Data Engineering, Infrastructure, Product, and other partner teams on cross-platform initiatives.

90 Days: Lead the design and delivery of key roadmap initiatives for the team..Influence technical direction across teams and mentor engineers on distributed systems and platform engineering best practices.Establish clear architectural recommendations for the next phase of the platform’s evolution.

In 90 days, you will have a detailed understanding of the Real-Time Analytics Platform and its role within PlayStation’s broader data ecosystem. You will be comfortable owning complex distributed systems initiatives, partnering closely with Product and Engineering teams, and driving large-scale solutions from architecture through production delivery.

In addition, this role is eligible for SIE’s top-tier benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, matching 401(k), paid time off, wellness program and coveted employee discounts for Sony products. This role also may be eligible for a bonus package. Click here to learn more.

jobs.title: Synthetic Chemist
jobs.description:
Inductive Bio is an AI medicinal chemistry partner. We build virtual labs that help drug discovery teams make better decisions, faster, across the full Design-Make-Test-Analyze (DMTA) cycle.

Our platform includes Beacon-2 ADMET prediction models, human dose projection tools, and Indy, an AI medicinal chemistry assistant. Through partnerships with CROs, we also offer innovative synthesis approaches, direct-to-dose testing, and cost-effective Tier 1 ADME panels that enable initial human PK projection, closing the loop from computational design to experimental validation. Together, these capabilities power dozens of small molecule and beyond-rule-of-five programs for biotech and pharma partners.

We've raised $30M from Obvious Ventures, a16z Bio + Health, and Lux Capital, and were selected for a $21M ARPA-H CATALYST award to develop next-generation toxicity models.

About the Role

We are seeking an accomplished Synthetic Chemist to help build the experimental chemistry capabilities behind Inductive's AI-forward drug discovery platform. This role combines medicinal chemistry strategy with hands-on synthesis expertise to design better compounds, solve challenging synthetic problems, and accelerate Design-Make-Test-Analyze workflows.

You'll play a key role in bridging computational design and experimental chemistry, bringing practical synthesis expertise to both the lab and the digital tools we're building.

This is an onsite role based in Boston, with regular visits to our local lab, reporting directly to our VP, Head of Medicinal Chemistry.

What You'll Do

 - Apply your synthetic chemistry expertise to design, optimize, and troubleshoot synthetic routes across a diverse range of medicinal chemistry programs.

 - Translate your practical knowledge into digital workflows that optimize synthetic routes, identify reaction conditions, streamline CRO communication, and track compound progress.

 - Oversee synthesis activities with CRO partners, leveraging both your chemistry expertise and Inductive's technology to deliver high-quality compounds efficiently.

 - Train and mentor laboratory technicians, ensuring reactions are executed safely, effectively, and reproducibly.

 - Develop strategic approaches to compound and intermediate supply, including route optimization and scale-up to support ongoing medicinal chemistry exploration.

 - Collaborate with medicinal chemists, computational scientists, and engineers to improve how compounds are designed, synthesized, and tested.

 - Help shape a new approach to drug discovery by integrating hands-on chemistry expertise with AI-powered tools and workflows.

What We're Looking For

 - A passion for advancing medicinal chemistry programs through practical, hands-on synthetic chemistry.

 - Deep knowledge of modern synthetic methods, with a strong understanding of what works in practice at the bench.

 - A track record of solving complex synthetic challenges across diverse chemotypes, reaction types, and scales.

 - Experience mentoring junior chemists or technicians and sharing practical laboratory expertise.

 - Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to clearly articulate synthetic strategies and troubleshoot challenges with cross-functional teams.

 - Demonstrated experience managing synthesis CROs, including both FTE-based teams and fee-for-service projects across multiple partners.

 - Strategic thinking around material supply, including when to optimize routes, develop key intermediates, and scale synthesis to support program needs.

 - Curiosity about emerging technologies and an interest in applying AI agents and digital tools to improve synthesis workflows.

Bonus Points

 - Experience overseeing scale-up synthesis for in vivo toxicology studies or other late-stage drug discovery activities.

 - Experience applying AI, automation, or digital tools to synthetic chemistry workflows.

 - Experience working at the intersection of medicinal chemistry, computational chemistry, and experimental drug discovery.

Working at Inductive

At Inductive Bio, we know that the people on the team are what make us great. We offer competitive salary and equity-based compensation; comprehensive healthcare benefits (including dental and vision); and the opportunity to grow along with a rapidly scaling company. We are a passionate, kind, and mature team. Working at a fast-growing startup is not always a 9-5 job, but we believe that our employees should have full lives beyond their career.

jobs.title: Electrical Engineer, Power Systems Analysis

AECOM seeks an Electrical Engineer, Power Systems Analysis specializing in power system studies for grid-interconnected and islanded power generation projects. In this role, you will be responsible for leading and executing comprehensive analytical studies that assess the performance and reliability of power systems.

AECOM's broad technical capabilities, global footprint and experience in executing large scale projects uniquely position us to lead in traditional steam, thermal power generation and advanced nuclear technologies. This includes being a part of the first-of-a-kind program with AECOM partners advancing the innovative stellarator technology to the world.

https://aecom.com/press-releases/aecom-establishes-partnership-with-type-one-energy-to-provide-design-engineering-services-for-its-innovative-stellarator-fusion-power-plant-infinity-two/

For this role, AECOM offers the freedom and flexibility to work remotely and/or be located at a variety of Energy offices located in multiple locations across the United States.

The successful candidate will have a strong understanding and extensive experience in electrical engineering, controls design, and power generation projects.

The responsibilities of this role also include, but may not be limited to, the following:

• Responsible for the electrical engineering design work on assigned projects
• Serve as lead engineer on all size projects maintaining responsibility for deliverable development
• Coordination with the electrical design team to direct completion of engineering drawings (one-line diagrams, protection & control schemes, settings files, and metering/SCADA integration requirements)
• Perform steady-state and dynamic analyses, including load flow, short-circuit, contingency analysis, transient stability, frequency response, voltage stability, and motor starting.
• Conduct protection and coordination studies, relay settings, arc flash assessments, and grounding studies in compliance with applicable standards.
• Support interconnection applications including generator and inverter-based resources
• Execute islanded and microgrid analyses (black start, droop control, power-sharing, stability, protection, and resilience strategies).
• Develop and validate models (PSSE/PSLF/DIgSILENT PowerFactory, ETAP, SKM, ASPEN, PSCAD) and prepare comprehensive study reports and presentations.
• Evaluate and optimize solutions for renewables, battery energy storage, CHP, and conventional generation projects.
• Home office and field support of projects during construction, start-up, and commissioning
• Performs quality control reviews of work developed by others
• Collaborate closely with multi-disciplinary teams (mechanical, controls, civil/structural, and construction) to integrate study results into design packages.
• Participate in project and client meetings
• Interact with vendors, regulatory agencies and contractors
• Assist with internal and external presentations
• Occasional travel to client and/or project sites

DCS—Energy

AECOM’s Energy practice provides a wide range of services from consulting and engineering design to energy engineering, energy procurement and construction (EPC) for power, energy efficiency, and renewable energy clients. Our understanding of the big picture – and the interconnection between generation, distribution, storage, and the demand side of the meter – allows us to deliver holistic strategies that improve and modernize next generation energy infrastructure. We connect knowledge and experience across our global framework to bring together a unique combination of engineers, planners, scientists, and project managers who advance cleaner, secure, and more sustainable energy solutions.

MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS:

• BA/BS in Electrical Engineering + 6 years of related experience or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education
• Relevant experience in mechanical engineering for power generation facilities

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

• Masters Degree in Electrical Engineering
• Professional Engineer (P.E.) license
• 10+ years of experience in mechanical engineering for power generation facilities
• Experience in engineer and design of Combined Cycle Plants and Nuclear Generation Stations
• Expert familiarity with industry codes and standards (IEC, NFPA, NERC CIP).
• Experience with specifying electrical equipment and hardware
• Startup and Commissioning Field Experience
• Proficiency with power system modeling software packages: ETAP, SKM, PSCAD, PSSE, DIgSILENT Aspen, etc.
• Experience working in collaborative model environments (e.g. Navisworks, BIM 360)
• Demonstrated experience in participating in complex, multi-discipline programs/projects
• Successful experience working in remote and multi-discipline teams

• Sponsorship for US employment authorization is not available now or in the future for this position.
• Relocation is not available for this position.

At AECOM, we are committed to maintaining a secure and trustworthy recruitment process and take any fraudulent hiring activity seriously. To support this commitment, all newly hired employees are required to attend an in-person Day 1 onboarding at an AECOM office location as a condition of employment.

About AECOM

AECOM is proud to offer comprehensive benefits to meet the diverse needs of our employees. Depending on your employment status, AECOM benefits may include medical, dental, vision, life, AD&D, disability benefits, paid time off, leaves of absences, voluntary benefits, perks, flexible work options, well-being resources, employee assistance program, business travel insurance, service recognition awards, retirement savings plan, and employee stock purchase plan.

AECOM is the global infrastructure leader, committed to delivering a better world. As a trusted professional services firm powered by deep technical abilities, we solve our clients’ complex challenges in water, environment, energy, transportation and buildings. Our teams partner with public- and private-sector clients to create innovative, sustainable and resilient solutions throughout the project lifecycle – from advisory, planning, design and engineering to program and construction management. AECOM is a Fortune 500 firm that had revenue of $16.1 billion in fiscal year 2025. Learn more at aecom.com.

What makes AECOM a great place to work

You will be part of a global team that champions your growth and career ambitions. Work on groundbreaking projects - both in your local community and on a global scale - that are transforming our industry and shaping the future. With cutting-edge technology and a network of experts, you’ll have the resources to make a real impact. Our award-winning training and development programs are designed to expand your technical expertise and leadership skills, helping you build the career you’ve always envisioned. Here, you’ll find a welcoming workplace built on respect, collaboration and community—where you have the freedom to grow in a world of opportunity.

As an Equal Opportunity Employer, we believe in your potential and are here to help you achieve it. All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

About the role:

Vera Louisiana is seeking a full-time Research Analyst to provide a wide range of support for ongoing projects, including jail population reduction, increasing investment in thriving communities, and addressing Louisiana’s carceral impact at the parish and state level. The Research Analyst will be supervised primarily by the Associate Director of Research (ADR) with support and mentorship from the Senior Research Associate and will support completion of a variety of quantitative and qualitative research projects with other staff. This position will provide an opportunity to gain knowledge and experience in applied social justice research, in using research to advance advocacy goals, and in criminal legal systems in New Orleans and other parts of Louisiana. The Research Analyst will work primarily on qualitative research projects, which require independent coding and analysis, will have the opportunity to support and develop skills in qualitative coding and analysis, and will also occasionally perform tasks beyond research-specific assignments, including some advocacy and administrative work.

The Research Analyst collaborates with team members to advance project or initiative goals, by actively engaging in team meetings and program activities, and supports efforts to ensure Vera’s race equity and inclusion priorities are a core aspect of Vera’s research, including in methodological approaches, publications, hiring and staffing, and external and internal research communications.

1. Data collection, management, and analysis

• Support in-person data collection under the supervision of senior research staff

• Clean, code, and manage data (quant and/or qual) and codebooks, instruments, or other research materials

• Support quantitative and/or qualitative analysis of data and/or write up of methods and results

• Field rapid response data requests from team members and external partners, including quickly producing statistics or identifying and sharing existing research to provide evidence in support of advocacy materials and more

2. Write up/presentation of research

• Conduct background research and compile materials, including literature reviews

• Prepare, format, and draft portions of reports, slide decks, factsheets, and other products

• Prepare qualitative and/or quantitative data, statistics, background research, and data visualizations for reports and other products

3. Administrative Tasks

• Support in planning, preparing for, and taking notes at meetings, conference calls, webinars and conferences

• Manage and respond to emails from external partners who work with Vera

• Schedule and facilitate meetings

• Data entry tasks, including creating, updating, and maintaining spreadsheets and databases

• Support the logistical/event/research trip planning process as needed

4. Administrative Tasks

• Support in planning, preparing for, and taking notes at meetings, conference calls, webinars and conferences

• Manage and respond to emails from external partners who work with Vera

• Schedule and facilitate meetings

• Data entry tasks, including creating, updating, and maintaining spreadsheets and databases

• Support the logistical/event/research trip planning process as needed

What qualifications are we looking for?

Required:

• Bachelor’s degree social science, statistics, or computer science + up to 3 years of relevant experience. In lieu of a Bachelor’s degree, applicable work or life experience may be considered.

Preferred:

• Experience using mixed methods research in applied settings

• Experience creating data visualizations or infographics

• Lived experience as a person directly impacted by the criminal legal system

• A demonstrated commitment to racial justice, equity, and inclusion

• Deep understanding of the New Orleans and/or Louisiana carceral system

Knowledge, Skills, & Abilities you'll bring:

• Experience in quantitative research (e.g. completing a research project using quantitative methods).

• Coding experience for data analysis, preferably in R

• Ability to synthesize complex literature and share findings from existing research

• Skilled in writing findings from research in a manner that is easily understood by the general public

• Strong written and verbal communication skills

• Excellent organizational skills and careful attention to detail

• Developing ability with data visualization and presentation and a desire to learn more

• Spanish language proficiency a plus

• Proficient with Microsoft Office Suite, Zoom, Slack, and Asana or other cloud-based management software

Location:

Please note this role will report to our New Orleans, Louisiana office. Vera employees adhere to a hybrid schedule and are in-office on an alternating schedule that generally amounts to 10 days per month.

Compensation and Benefits:

The compensation range for this position is $64,000 - $67,000. In addition, this position is part of a bargaining unit represented by the Association of Legal Aid Attorneys (ALAA) UAW 2325. Actual salaries will vary depending on factors including but not limited to experience and performance. The salary range listed is just one component of Vera Institute’s total compensation package for employees. As an employer of choice in our field, supporting Vera staff - both personally and professionally - is a priority. To do this, we invest in the well-being of our staff through other rewards including merit pay, generous paid time off, a comprehensive health insurance plan, student loan repayment benefits, professional development training opportunities and up to $2,000 annual for education costs and fees relevant to Vera work, employer-funded retirement plan, and flexible time. To learn more about Vera’s benefits offerings, click here.

jobs.title: Senior Strategist, Federal Advocacy, Advocacy & Partnerships
jobs.description:
About the team:

Vera’s Advocacy & Partnerships department is responsible for coordinating the vision, strategy, and staff development across Vera’s initiatives to pass legislation, change policy, and create change at scale. We work to ensure that the goals of our advocacy campaigns align with the people and communities most impacted by criminal justice and immigration policies, and we collaborate with movement and advocacy partners to produce the knowledge and ideas needed to change policies and legislation at the right time.

Vera’s Advocacy & Partnerships department serves the following core functions:

• Providing state and local government and movement strategy guidance to Vera’s national and place-based initiatives, with a focus on lobbying, campaigns, and coalition work;

• Federal policy expertise to lead Vera’s advocacy strategies in Washington, D.C.;

• Vera Insights, a rapid-response data and evidence team responsible for developing and producing data and knowledge to key partners and audiences; and

• Coordination with Vera Action, Vera’s sister 501(c)(4) organization.

About the role:

The Senior Strategist, Federal Advocacy is a key member of Vera’s Advocacy & Partnerships department and serves as a strategist and advocate focused on advancing Vera’s federal policy priorities and defending against federal actions that threaten them. The Senior Strategist develops and executes federal advocacy strategies to advance legislation, federal budget and appropriations priorities, administrative policies, and other federal policy changes aligned with Vera’s goals.

The Senior Strategist monitors and analyzes the federal political and policy environment, identifies opportunities to advance Vera’s priorities, develops strategies to influence federal decision-makers, and builds relationships with congressional offices, federal agencies, national advocacy organizations, and other key stakeholders. This role will work closely with movement and coalition partners to build power and advance shared federal policy goals.

At a moment when federal policymakers are pushing a return to failed “tough-on-crime” policies, Vera’s role is to bring the data, evidence, and solutions about what works into federal policy debates, particularly with government and grasstops stakeholders. Vera's February 2026 platform, A New Federal Paradigm for Safety, Accountability, and Justice, reflects the kind of popular, evidence-based  federal solutions Vera champions, organized around six planks: strong, accountable policing; ending the overdose crisis; supporting strong mental health and deescalating crisis; tackling gun violence; safe streets and good quality of life; and a fairer, more accountable justice system. On immigration, Vera works to hold federal immigration enforcement accountable, expand access to deportation defense and universal legal representation for people facing deportation, and push back against the expansion of DHS’s power.

The Senior Strategist will serve as a lead strategist on assigned federal policy priorities, helping determine when and how Vera should engage in federal legislative, appropriations, regulatory, and administrative processes. The role requires strong political judgment, an understanding of federal policymaking, excellent communication skills, and the ability to move complex advocacy campaigns forward in a dynamic environment.

1. Develop and execute federal advocacy strategies and campaigns

• Work with the Director of Federal Advocacy and other members of the Advocacy & Partnerships department to develop and execute federal advocacy strategies for Vera’s core issues and policy priorities, including legislation and policy change related to safety, accountability, and justice.

• Manage assigned federal advocacy campaigns from strategy development through implementation, including coordinating tactics, timelines, partners, and deliverables.

• Develop and execute bipartisan congressional strategies by identifying key decision-makers, committees, legislative opportunities, and champions, while building and maintaining relationships with congressional offices and federal policymakers to advance Vera’s policy priorities.

• Lead or support the development, drafting, tracking, and advancement of federal legislation, including identifying legislative opportunities, shaping bill language, developing legislative strategies, and supporting efforts to secure congressional support.

• Develop and execute federal budget and appropriations advocacy strategies, including tracking the federal budget and appropriations process, identifying funding priorities and threats, developing requests and recommendations, and engaging relevant congressional offices and committees.

• Identify and pursue opportunities to influence federal regulations, executive actions, agency policies, guidance, and other administrative decisions.

• Monitor federal legislative, budgetary, regulatory, administrative, and political developments and assess their implications for Vera’s priorities and advocacy strategy.

• Translate political and policy intelligence into actionable recommendations, identifying strategic openings, potential risks, and appropriate moments for engagement.

• Develop advocacy materials, including policy briefs, talking points, legislative recommendations, congressional materials, testimony, sign-on letters, and other communications designed to influence federal decision-makers.

• Collaborate with the Director of Federal Advocacy and the Chief Advocacy Officer to determine where Vera should engage, lead, partner, or strategically remain outside of federal campaigns and policy debates.

2. Federal coalition building, partnerships, and external engagement

• Build and maintain strategic relationships with national advocacy organizations, movement partners, grasstops and grassroots organizations, congressional offices, federal agencies, and other stakeholders relevant to Vera’s federal policy priorities.

• Identify, develop, and participate in federal coalitions that can advance Vera’s policy and legislative goals.

• Help develop and implement joint advocacy strategies with coalition and movement partners, including coordinated congressional engagement, public advocacy, legislative campaigns, and other tactics.

• Represent Vera in strategically important federal advocacy meetings, coalitions, briefings, congressional meetings, policy discussions, and other external spaces.

• Coordinate with national movement partners to identify opportunities for collective action and build broader support for federal policy priorities.

• Support strategic communications and public advocacy efforts designed to build momentum for federal policy change.

• Serve as a strategic connector between Vera and relevant federal advocacy networks, ensuring Vera is positioned to identify and respond to emerging federal policy opportunities.

3. Federal policy analysis, intelligence, and internal coordination

• Maintain a current understanding of federal legislative, budgetary, regulatory, administrative, and political developments relevant to Vera’s policy priorities.

• Produce concise, timely analysis and recommendations for Vera leadership and Advocacy & Partnerships colleagues on significant federal developments and opportunities for advocacy.

• Develop and maintain systems for tracking federal legislation, appropriations, regulatory and administrative developments, congressional activity, key relationships, coalition activity, and campaign progress.

• Collaborate with Vera’s policy, research, communications, and other relevant staff to ensure federal advocacy strategies are informed by Vera’s research, expertise, and policy analysis.

What qualifications are we looking for?

Required:

• Bachelor’s degree and 4+ years of relevant experience. In lieu of degree requirement, applicable work or life experience may be considered.

• Demonstrated experience working on criminal justice, immigration, public safety, or related public policy issues.

• At least 3 years of experience planning and leading federal advocacy campaigns. Including managing complex campaigns and projects from strategy development through implementation.

• Experience developing and implementing advocacy strategies involving multiple stakeholders, decision-makers, and advocacy partners.

• Demonstrated ability to analyze political and policy developments and translate them into advocacy strategy.

• Experience developing advocacy materials, including legislative recommendations, talking points, policy briefs, testimony, congressional materials, and other advocacy communications.

Preferred:

• 3+ years of issue advocacy and community organizing experience.

• Experience building and/or leading coalitions in partnership with national, grasstops, and grassroots organizations.

• Experience working directly with congressional offices, congressional committees, federal agencies, or other federal policymakers.

• Experience with federal appropriations, budget advocacy, or fiscal policy.

• Experience developing or advancing federal legislation, regulations, executive actions, or administrative policy.

• Experience working on criminal legal system or immigration policy at the federal level.

• 2+ years of electoral political experience and organizing experience.

Knowledge, Skills, & Abilities you'll bring:

• Strong knowledge of federal advocacy strategy, policymaking, and power building.

• Demonstrated understanding of Congress and the federal legislative process, including congressional committees, legislative vehicles, hearings, and congressional decision-making.

• Demonstrated understanding of the federal budget, appropriations, and administrative processes.

• Strong understanding of congressional decision-making, committee structures, legislative strategy, and federal appropriations.

• Strong political and strategic judgment, including the ability to identify opportunities, anticipate challenges, assess political dynamics, and adapt advocacy strategies as circumstances change.

• Ability to develop and maintain relationships with congressional offices, federal agencies, coalition partners, and other external stakeholders.

• Ability to research, synthesize, and communicate complex policy and political information clearly and effectively.

• Excellent writing, oral communication, and presentation skills.

• Ability to issue-spot and problem-solve across federal policy and advocacy strategy, including proactively and creatively developing tactics, resources, and tools.

• Ability to prioritize and manage multiple activities in a fast-paced environment.

• Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively with a national team while independently managing responsibilities and external relationships.

• Ability to work effectively in a highly collaborative and politically dynamic environment.

• A deep commitment to Vera’s mission to end mass incarceration, fight for immigrant rights, bring dignity to people behind bars, and help build safe, thriving communities.

Location:

Please note this role will report to our Washington, DC office. Vera employees adhere to a hybrid schedule and are in-office on an alternating schedule that generally amounts to 10 days per month.

Compensation and Benefits:

The compensation range for this position is $105,000-110,000. In addition, this position is part of a bargaining unit represented by the Association of Legal Aid Attorneys (ALAA) UAW 2325. Actual salaries will vary depending on factors including but not limited to experience and performance. The salary range listed is just one component of Vera Institute’s total compensation package for employees. As an employer of choice in our field, supporting Vera staff - both personally and professionally - is a priority. To do this, we invest in the well-being of our staff through other rewards including merit pay, generous paid time off, a comprehensive health insurance plan, student loan repayment benefits, professional development training opportunities and up to $2,000 annual for education costs and fees relevant to Vera work, employer-funded retirement plan, and flexible time. To learn more about Vera’s benefits offerings, click here.

jobs.title: Technical Support Engineer
jobs.description:
L3 TECHNICAL SUPPORT ENGINEER, ENTERPRISE NETWORKING AND AV SOLUTIONS

Location: Remote, Canada (British Columbia preferred)
Department: Customer Support and Services (CSS)
Reports To: Manager, L3 Technical Support

About the Role

NETGEAR is looking for a highly skilled, customer-focused L3 Technical Support Engineer to join our growing Enterprise Networking and AV technical support team. This is a remote position based in Canada, with a preference for candidates in British Columbia. You'll work hours that line up with Pacific Time to support our North America customers.

You'll be the escalation point for L1 and L2 support. Working with our engineering teams, you'll resolve complex networking and AV-over-IP issues for enterprise customers, MSPs, and integrators. You'll support NETGEAR's switches, WiFi access points, security gateways, and network management solutions, both cloud and on-premises. In this post-sales role, you'll represent NETGEAR to our customers, bringing strong technical skills and excellent customer management to a fast-paced, high-growth environment.

Key Responsibilities

 - Serve as the technical escalation point for Enterprise Networking and AV customers, working with them directly by phone whenever possible

 - Diagnose and resolve complex technical issues involving:
   
   - Layer 2 switching and Layer 3 routing
   
   - QoS, IGMP, and STP
   
   - Network and AV-over-IP hardware
   
   - Wireless networking
   
   - AV protocols and interoperability (Dante, NDI, AES67, and others)
   
   - Cloud-based and on-premises management platforms

 - Work with engineering and product teams to resolve complex issues and bugs, and share feedback that improves the customer experience

 - Replicate issues and validate fixes hands-on in lab environments

 - Document solutions, root causes, and workarounds in the knowledge base

 - Stay current on emerging networking and AV technologies, including NETGEAR product roadmaps and firmware updates

 - Contribute to proactive support work, such as support guides, training for lower-tier support teams, and customer-facing webinars and documentation

What You Bring

 - 4+ years of experience in customer-facing technical support, network operations, or field support, ideally in enterprise or AV-over-IP switching environments

 - Fluent written and spoken English, with the ability to explain complex technical concepts to customers at any level of technical expertise

 - Extensive knowledge of networking protocols and topologies

 - Hands-on expertise with:
   
   - VLANs, QoS, STP/RSTP, and Ethernet switching protocols
   
   - Wireless networking deployment and troubleshooting
   
   - Routing protocols and troubleshooting
   
   - IGMP Snooping, Querier, and multicast traffic optimization
   
   - CLI troubleshooting tools, port mirroring, and packet capture analysis

 - Strong working knowledge of Wireshark

 - Experience supporting or deploying NETGEAR switches or similar platforms (Cisco, Extreme, Aruba)

 - Strong skills with technical documentation, ticketing systems, and remote diagnostic tools

Nice to Have

 - Familiarity with ProAV systems and tools such as Dante Controller, Q-SYS, NDI Studio Monitor, AMX, or Crestron NVX

 - Experience supporting AV system integrators, event production, or ProAV deployments

 - Industry certifications such as NETGEAR Certified, CCNA, CWNA, Dante Level 2+, or AVIXA CTS

 - A track record of working remotely and independently

Who You Are

 - A confident problem solver who handles escalations calmly and professionally

 - Committed to customer satisfaction, with a consultative approach

 - A clear, effective communicator with customers, partners, and internal teams

 - Detail-oriented, with strong organization and documentation habits

 - Collaborative across Support, Engineering, and Product teams

 - Flexible with your hours when global customers need support

Company Statement/Values:  

At NETGEAR, we are on a mission to unleash the full potential of connectivity with intelligent solutions that delight and protect. We turn ideas into innovative networking products that connect people, power businesses, and advance the way we live.  

We're a performance-driven, talented and connected team that's committed to delivering world-class products for our customers. As a company, we value our employees as the most essential building blocks of our success. And as teammates, we commit to taking our work to the Next Gear by living our values: we Dare to Transform the future, Connect and Delight our customers, Communicate Courageously with each other and collaborate to Win It Together. You’ll find our values woven through our processes, present in our decisions, and celebrated throughout our culture. 

We strive to attract top talent and create a great workplace where people feel engaged, inspired, challenged, proud and respected. If you are creative, forward-thinking, passionate about technology and are looking for a rewarding career to make an impact, then you've got what it takes to succeed at NETGEAR. Join our network and help us shape the future of connectivity. 



NETGEAR hires based on merit. All qualified applicants will receive equal consideration for employment. All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

jobs.title: Director, Solutions Consultant
jobs.location: New York, New York, United States
jobs.description:
VTS is seeking a Director, Solutions Consultant, to assist and translate new business opportunities into a successful deployment plan across VTS — the platform that extends VTS into asset management and leasing.

This role sits at the intersection of sales, solution design, and implementation readiness. Once an opportunity is qualified, the Solutions Consultant becomes the solutions expert alongside the Account Executive — translating a customer’s needs into a tailored solution and, once the deal is won, into a complete solution design and implementation plan that hands off cleanly to the Implementation team. You will work predominantly through our major channel partners to start, expanding to the direct channel and other commercial clients over time, and partner closely with our sales, product, and account management teams.

Unlike a traditional pre-sales engineer focused only on the demonstration, or an implementation manager focused only on delivery, this position helps manage the full arc of solution implementation preparedness — from qualified opportunity, through solution design, to a clean handoff to implementation, with continued check-ins through launch.

This is a highly visible, senior individual-contributor role based in our New York office.

** Please note that this opportunity is located in New York, NY, and requires this hire to work from our office 4 days a week. **

What You'll Do

• Partner with the Account Executive as the solutions expert for complex and strategic deals, acting as the subject matter expert and partnering with customers to drive maximum value from our products

• Develop expert-level command of the feature set and tailor product messaging and demonstrations to each customer’s workflows and goals

• Solution discovery: take ambiguous, complex requirements, define them with customers and stakeholders, and shape them into a clear, cohesive solution

• Support our Account Executives with business and technical requirements, solution positioning, scoping, and alignment

• Aggregate everything learned during the sale into a single solution design — requirements, the technologies and features being deployed, and the rollout schedule — documented in the deal journal

• Produce a complete, unambiguous handoff package so the Implementation team can execute without rework

• Review the plan with Implementation at kickoff and stay engaged through deployment with defined check-in points to keep projects on track

• Collaborate day-to-day with Sales, Product, QA — primarily in Salesforce, with exposure to tools such as Jira and Airtable

• Serve as a trusted advisor to customers and internal stakeholders, and evangelize the vision across the commercial real estate ecosystem

What We're Looking For

• 3–5+ years in a pre-sales or solutioning role — Solutions Consultant, Sales Engineer, Technical Account Manager, Pre-Sales Consultant, or a Customer Success Manager ready to move into pre-sales

• SaaS background required, with a proven track record of playing the solutions/pre-sales role well and telling a compelling product-to-value story (the industry it was in matters less than how well you did it)

• Exceptional client-facing and facilitation skills — personable, credible with executives, and able to command a room and drive a meeting

• Highly process and project management oriented, able to manage complex solution definition end-to-end and bring structure to ambiguity

• Strong problem-solving skills, with the ability to translate technical capability into measurable business value

• Ability to ramp quickly on the platform

• Comfortable working in Salesforce; exposure to implementation or ticketing tools such as Jira or Airtable a plus

• Commercial real estate or proptech experience a plus

• New York–based, able to work from our office and travel up to ~25% (a few days per month for client meetings and QBRs)

What VTS Values & How We Show It

• Strive for Excellence - We know your potential is unlimited. Take advantage of our executive coaches and our training and career development programs available to all employees!

• Be Customer Obsessed - We’re employee obsessed too! VTS offers competitive compensation, comprehensive health benefits (including dental and vision), pre-tax commuter benefits, and a 401(k) plan. Not to mention the fun stuff - quarterly happy hours, wellness events, clubs, and team lunches!

• Be Curious - Benefit from a culture that promotes new learning. VTS offers an education stipend to all employees!

• Move as One - We work in an open floor plan to promote cross-functional collaboration.

• Take Ownership - Be an owner of the company you’re building with our equity packages.

• Appreciate the Difference - VTS embraces and celebrates diversity. We understand the importance of a strong work-life balance. We offer a flexible PTO policy, generous family leave program, and more!

ABOUT VTS

VTS is the only AI-driven technology platform enabling intelligent real estate by unifying industry professionals, investors, and their customers at scale. In 2013, VTS revolutionized commercial real estate leasing operations with what is now VTS Lease. Today, VTS AI is the largest first-party insights and collaboration engine in the industry, transforming how strategic decisions are made and executed by the real estate industry globally.

With the VTS Platform, consisting of VTS Lease, VTS Market, VTS Activate, and VTS Data, every stakeholder in real estate is given real-time market information and workflow tools to do their job with unparalleled speed and intelligence. VTS is the global leader, with more than 60% of Class A office space in the U.S., and 13 billion square feet of office, residential, retail, and industrial space is managed through the platform worldwide. VTS is utilized by over 45,000 professionals and over 1.2 million total users each day, including industry-leading customers such as Blackstone, Brookfield Properties, LaSalle Investment Management, Hines, BXP, Oxford Properties, JLL, and CBRE.

VTS maintains offices in New York City, London, Toronto, Chicago.

To learn more about VTS and view our open roles, visit us at vts.com or follow us on Instagram (@WeAreVTS) or LinkedIn.

Pay Transparency

At VTS, we pride ourselves on articulating a clear and transparent philosophy around equitable, impartial compensation that will allow us to recruit and retain an exceptional team. The base salary is market-driven at the time of offer and is based on tier 1 market data. The salary for this role will range between $140,000 and $180,000 and is determined by several factors, including your skills, prior relevant experience, quality of interviews, leveling, and geography. There is a bonus structure for the position that will bring the OTE (on target earnings) to $200,000 - $240,000 depending on the base salary agreed upon and achievement to goals.

EEO Guidelines

VTS embraces diversity and equal opportunity in a serious way. We are committed to building a team that represents a variety of backgrounds, perspectives, and skills. The more inclusive we are, the better our work will be.

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines. For more information about what we collect and how we use it, please refer to the Candidate Privacy Statement.

If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation at any time during the recruitment process, please let us know at ta@vts.com

Privacy Policy

jobs.title: Lead Engineer, Zonal ECU Design Responsible Engineer
jobs.description:
Here at Scout Motors, we're carrying forward the heritage of one of the most iconic American vehicles in history. A vehicle dating back to 1960. One that forged the path for future generations of rugged SUVs and trucks and will do so once again.

But Scout is more than just a brand, it’s a legacy steeped in a culture of exploration, caretaking, and hard work.

The Scout brand is all about respect. Respect for the past and the future by taking an iconic American brand that hasn’t been around for a while, electrifying it, digitizing it, and loading it with American innovation. Respect for communities by creating a company that stands for its people and its customers. Respect for both work and play, with vehicles that are equally at home at a camp site, a job site, or on a Tuesday commute. And respect for our customers by developing two powertrains that meet their requirements — an all-electric powertrain as well as the Harvester™ range extender powertrain which includes a built-in gas-powered generator with an estimated 500 miles of combined range.

At Scout Motors, we empower our talented, inclusive, and entrepreneurial teams to innovate. What makes a Scout employee? Someone who is a visionary and a leader, who seeks new paths and shares lessons learned. A knowledgeable doer who collaborates across the company to build better. A go-getter with unrivaled passion.

Join us at Scout Motors and be part of shaping the future of transportation. If you're ready to drive change and make history, apply now!

What you’ll do

Become part of an iconic brand that is set to revolutionize the electric pick-up truck & rugged SUV marketplace by achieving the following:

• Own the end-to-end design and release strategy for zonal ECUs from concept through production launch, exercising independent technical judgment on significant and unique hardware issues that may affect the broader Vehicle Software & Electrical Engineering function.

• Serve as the subject matter expert for zonal ECU hardware, coordinating across Body, Drive, Energy, electrical architecture, software, validation, manufacturing, purchasing, quality, and suppliers to convey advanced technical information and align diverse stakeholders.

• Define, govern, and approve zonal ECU hardware requirements and technical tradeoffs, including power distribution, thermal management, signal integrity, diagnostics, cybersecurity interfaces, packaging, cost, quality, and timing.

• Lead ECU architecture and design reviews, DFMEAs, validation strategies, and technical decision forums; evaluate incomplete information and competing program priorities to recommend effective solutions.

• Ensure compliance with applicable automotive standards and internal engineering requirements, including ISO 26262, EMC, ESD, cybersecurity, and manufacturing readiness expectations.

• Direct supplier technical activities and deliverables, establish performance expectations, resolve escalated technical issues, and ensure components and systems achieve program cost, timing, quality, and launch targets.

• Lead resolution of cross-functional and cross-domain issues during build events, validation, launch, and lifecycle change management, including root-cause analysis, risk assessment, recovery planning, and technical arbitration.

• Contribute to company and functional objectives by establishing scalable zonal ECU engineering practices, lessons learned, design standards, and continuous-improvement priorities.

• Provide technical direction and mentoring to engineers and extended team members as needed while working with a high degree of independence.

• Proactively assess consumer and vehicle-system impacts and recommend zonal ECU improvements that strengthen performance, reliability, manufacturability, serviceability, and customer experience.

• Contribute ECU technical requirements and readiness input to production-facility and manufacturing-process design for Scout trucks and SUVs.

Location & Travel Expectations:

• This role will be based out of the Scout Motors location in Novi, Michigan.

• This role requires 4-5 days per week in the office, with regular in-person meetings and events.

• Applicants should expect that the role will require the ability to convene with Scout colleagues in person and travel to participate in events on behalf of the company from time to time.

What you’ll bring

We expect all Scout employees to have integrity, curiosity, resourcefulness, and strive to exhibit a positive attitude, as well as a growth mindset. You’ll be comfortable with change and flexible in a fast-paced, high-growth environment. You’ll take a collaborative approach to achieve ambitious goals. Here's what else you'll bring:

• Bachelor's or master's degree in electrical engineering, combined electrical/mechanical engineering, or a relevant field.

• 12+ years of progressive experience in ECU hardware development and release, including leadership of critical ECU programs from concept through production launch.

• Demonstrated success launching critical ECUs into production, such as body electrical, powertrain, battery, drive unit, power distribution, zonal, or centralized compute systems.

• Recognized subject matter expertise in ECU hardware architecture, PCB design, component selection, thermal and power analysis, signal integrity, manufacturing, and validation.

• Demonstrated ability to resolve significant and unique technical issues, evaluate intangible and competing factors, and exercise independent judgment on decisions that may affect a broader engineering function.

jobs.title: Sr. Manager Network Finance & Strategy
jobs.description:
Legend Biotech is a global biotechnology company dedicated to treating and, one day, curing life-threatening diseases. Headquartered in Bridgewater, New Jersey, we are advancing the next generation of cell therapy through a portfolio of innovative technologies, including autologous, allogeneic, and in vivo cell therapy approaches. Our research spans chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T), T-cell receptor (TCR-T), natural killer (NK) cell-based therapies, and other emerging platforms designed to transform the treatment of serious diseases. From our global network of research and development sites, we are committed to discovering and developing safe, effective, and cutting-edge therapies for patients worldwide.

Legend Biotech entered into a global collaboration agreement with Johnson & Johnson to jointly develop and commercialize CARVYKTI® (ciltacabtagene autoleucel; cilta-cel). Through this strategic partnership, we combine complementary expertise and capabilities to advance innovative immunotherapies for patients living with multiple myeloma.

Legend Biotech is seeking a Sr. Manager Network Finance & Strategy as part of the Finance team based in Bridgewater, NJ.

Role Overview

The Senior Manager, Network Finance & Strategy is a strategic finance leader responsible for financial planning, performance management, and decision support across Legend Biotech’s global manufacturing and supply network. The role provides an integrated financial perspective across manufacturing sites, external manufacturing partners, supply-chain functions, and portfolio programs.

Reporting to the Director, Supply Chain Finance, this position leads the financial evaluation of manufacturing network strategies, major investments, capacity decisions, automation initiatives, and gross-margin opportunities. The Senior Manager partners with Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Quality, MSAT, Engineering, Procurement, and Finance leadership to translate operational strategies into clear financial implications and recommendations.

The position also leads Network FP&A and supports the continued expansion of Supply Chain Finance beyond CARVYKTI to Legend’s broader pipeline. The role oversees consolidated planning and performance management while developing the financial frameworks, analytics, and team capabilities required to support future growth and commercialization.

Key Responsibilities

Network Strategy and Decision Support

• Lead the financial evaluation of manufacturing network strategies, including capacity expansion, volume allocation, product transfers, sourcing alternatives, and network configuration decisions.

• Develop scenario analyses that assess COGM, gross margin, capital requirements, cash flow, operational risk, and long-term financial implications.

• Serve as the primary Finance partner for strategic network-capacity planning and provide clear recommendations to support leadership decisions.

Strategic Investments and Business Cases

• Lead financial evaluations for automation, capacity expansion, technology investments, new facilities, and other manufacturing and supply-chain initiatives.

• Develop robust business cases incorporating NPV, ROI, payback, cash flow, depreciation, COGM, gross-margin impact, and sensitivity analysis.

• Lead the financial assessment of make-versus-buy, internal-versus-external manufacturing, CMO sourcing, and manufacturing-footprint decisions.

Gross Margin and Network Competitiveness

• Lead network-level financial analysis supporting long-term gross-margin expansion, manufacturing productivity, and cost competitiveness.

• Partner with Site Finance and operational leaders to identify, evaluate, prioritize, and track cross-site productivity and cost-improvement opportunities.

• Develop financial roadmaps connecting volume growth, operational improvements, automation, network optimization, and capital investment to long-term margin objectives.

Portfolio Manufacturing Finance

• Provide strategic Finance support for manufacturing and supply-chain decisions associated with pipeline products and future commercialization.

• Evaluate product economics, financial flows, manufacturing locations, capacity requirements, sourcing strategies, and investment timing for new programs.

• Integrate pipeline assumptions into manufacturing-network strategy, capital planning, and the long-range financial outlook.

Network FP&A Leadership

• Lead consolidated budgeting, forecasting, long-range planning, performance management, and reporting across the manufacturing and supply network.

• Oversee the Manager, Network FP&A in coordinating site submissions, maintaining planning models, consolidating results, and preparing management reporting.

• Challenge financial and operational assumptions and synthesize results into clear insights, risks, opportunities, and recommendations for leadership.

Executive Business Partnership

• Serve as a trusted Finance advisor to Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Quality, MSAT, Engineering, Procurement, and Finance leadership.

• Represent Supply Chain Finance in relevant operating, planning, governance, and leadership forums and act as a delegate to the Director, Supply Chain Finance when appropriate.

• Translate complex operational and financial information into concise, decision-oriented recommendations for senior leaders.

Finance Transformation and Analytics

• Establish priorities for Network Finance transformation, including planning models, dashboards, reporting automation, advanced analytics, and scalable data solutions.

• Partner with Finance, IT, and data teams to improve the availability, quality, governance, and use of manufacturing and supply-chain data.

• Drive standardization and automation to reduce manual processes and improve the speed, reliability, and decision usefulness of financial insights.

Team Leadership and Development

• Lead, coach, and develop the Network FP&A team, establishing clear objectives, responsibilities, and performance expectations.

• Build team capabilities in manufacturing finance, strategic modeling, analytics, executive communication, and business partnership.

• Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, continuous improvement, and high-quality financial analysis.

• The Senior Manager, Network Finance & Strategy works closely with the Director, Supply Chain Finance; Manager, Network FP&A; Site Finance leaders; Global Supply Chain Accounting; Corporate FP&A; Commercial Finance; Manufacturing; Supply Chain; Quality; MSAT; Engineering; Procurement; Clinical Supply; Corporate Accounting; Tax; IT; and data and analytics teams.

Requirements

• Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, Economics, or a related field required.

• Advanced degree and/or relevant professional accounting/finance qualification preferred.

• Significant progressive experience in FP&A, manufacturing finance, supply-chain finance, strategic finance, or a related discipline.

• Demonstrated experience leading complex financial planning, strategic modeling, business-case development, and executive decision support.

• Experience supporting manufacturing-network decisions, capital investments, automation, capacity expansion, or external-manufacturing strategies preferred.

• Experience within pharmaceutical, biotechnology, cell therapy, medical technology, or another regulated manufacturing environment preferred.

• Demonstrated experience leading employees and influencing senior stakeholders across functions and geographies.

• Strong knowledge of manufacturing economics, COGM, gross margin, capacity planning, inventory, productivity, and capital investment.

• Advanced financial modeling and business-case development capabilities.

• Strong FP&A, forecasting, long-range planning, performance-management, and analytical skills.

• Ability to translate complex analysis into clear executive recommendations.

• Strong business-partnering and influencing skills across functions, sites, and leadership levels.

jobs.title: Head of Product Led Growth
jobs.description:
About Re:Build

At Re:Build, our mission is to ensure the next generation of important products are made, at scale, in America. We are laying the foundation for a better future for our customers, employees, and communities by revitalizing America's manufacturing base and creating meaningful jobs across the country, including in historically deindustrialized regions.

We operate a sophisticated, end-to-end manufacturing platform that partners with industrial companies and innovators to take products from first concept to full-scale production in critical verticals including aerospace and defense, electrification, medical, energy and environment, and robotics and automation.

The way we operate is as meaningful as the work we do. It's guided by The Re:Build Way, 16 principles that shape how we collaborate with each other, partner with our customers and vendors, and give to the communities where we operate. The Re:Build Way principles

Re:Build is building Livewire, a launchpad business bringing AI-native software to intuitive wire harness design and manufacturing. The product is real, customers are already using it, and there's still a lot to learn about how the growth engine should work; that's where this role comes in.

We're looking for a hands-on product growth leader who can connect the whole customer journey: how the right users find Livewire, what gets them into the product, what gets them to real value, what brings them back, and what eventually gets them to pay. You'll work closely with Product and also partner with Marketing, Sales, RevOps, and Customer Success. Together, you will make that journey measurable and keep a consistent flow of experiments. These experiments will help turn what you learn into better product and growth decisions.

This is a builder role. You should be just as comfortable looking at product behavior as acquisition data, enjoy running experiments, want to talk to users, and be energized by the fact that there isn't a mature growth playbook waiting for you — because you'll help build it. You'll likely start with few or no direct reports. Instead, you will guide external firms, contractors, and internal specialists. See that as an opportunity rather than a limitation.

What You Get To Do

• Own the growth journey from acquisition through activation, lifecycle and conversion.

• Build a clear view of the customer journey; who's converting, where they get stuck, and whether they're reaching real value.

• Run a steady cadence of experiments across acquisition, onboarding, product experience, lifecycle and conversion.

• Partner with Product to turn user insights into a faster path to value.

• Build the measurement and operating rhythm that helps the team learn and decide faster.

• Drive conversion, retention and expansion with Sales, RevOps and Customer Success.

• Shape positioning and messaging based on customer insight, in partnership with Marketing.

• Direct agencies and specialists to move faster, without outsourcing the thinking.

What You Bring To The Team

• Experience in product growth, PLG, lifecycle marketing or a similar role; and you know growth doesn't stop at signup.

• Hands-on experience designing and running experiments, including with imperfect data and small samples.

• Strong partnership with Product, using customer and product data to drive decisions.

• Comfort operating with high autonomy and limited infrastructure.

• Strong quantitative skills funnels, cohorts, conversion and experiment analysis.

• Familiarity with product analytics, CRM/marketing automation, web analytics and experimentation tools.

• Preferred: product-led, self-service or digital commerce experience. Wire harness/CAD/manufacturing expertise not required.

Preferred Qualifications

• Product-led, self-service, digital commerce or online buying experience.

• Domain expertise in wire harnesses, CAD or manufacturing is not required; what matters is the ability to learn a technical customer and workflow quickly.

Additional Information

This is a sedentary role in a standard office environment, with occasional air and car travel. The working assumption is a standard full-time schedule with flexibility to collaborate closely with Product, Marketing and other Re:Build teams.

This is a chance to build, not inherit. Livewire is early enough that the important questions aren't all answered yet; which users get the most value, what makes them change how they work, where they get stuck, and what turns early usage into a lasting habit and commercial relationship. The Head of Product Growth will sit right in the middle of that work, close to Product, with significant influence over how Livewire's growth system gets built.

Compensation (Exempt)

The base salary range for this position is $120,223.20 - $214,598.41 per year. This range represents the Company’s good faith estimate of the base compensation for this role at the time of posting.  Actual compensation will be determined based on several factors, including but not limited to proven experience, skills, qualifications, internal equity, and geographic location. In addition to base salary, this role may be eligible for annual incentive compensation and/or long-term incentives, subject to Company plans. The Company offers a comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental, vision, retirement, paid time off, and other benefits.

The BIG payoff

We are a company who is going to make a difference in the industries and the areas where we choose to operate.    Every employee of Re:Build will share ownership in the company and will share in the financial rewards of the success we achieve together, at all levels of the company!

We want to work with people that reflect the communities in which we operate

We do not discriminate based upon race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, veteran status, marital status, parental status, cultural background, organizational level, work styles, tenure and life experiences. Or for any other reason.

jobs.description:
At Kodiak Solutions, we’re dedicated to transforming the healthcare industry through cutting-edge, technology-driven solutions. We specialize in healthcare finance, unclaimed property, risk management, and revenue cycle management, helping healthcare organizations streamline complex financial operations. Our mission is to simplify and optimize processes, so healthcare providers can focus on delivering excellent patient care.

Position Summary

The Inpatient DRG Validator plays an integral role within Kodiak’s Revenue Integrity Optimization team, helping healthcare organizations improve coding accuracy, compliance, quality, and reimbursement. Working alongside an experienced, U.S.-based team, Validators perform comprehensive inpatient coding and clinical validation reviews across both MS-DRG and APR-DRG methodologies.

DRG validation at Kodiak goes beyond traditional inpatient coding review, incorporating broader clinical and quality considerations such as Hospital-Acquired Conditions (HACs), Patient Safety Indicators (PSIs), and Elixhauser measures. This expanded approach provides Validators exposure to a diverse and evolving range of coding, clinical quality, and revenue integrity concepts while contributing meaningful value to the healthcare organizations we serve.

This is a production-focused role with established productivity, quality, and performance expectations suited for individuals who thrive in being part of a high performing team environment. Successful team members consistently meet defined performance standards while maintaining a high degree of accuracy and attention to detail.

Kodiak is committed to creating a collaborative, supportive, and highly engaged team environment where people can do meaningful work, build their expertise, and enjoy being part of a growing business. As the DRG Validation practice continues to expand, team members have opportunities to broaden their capabilities, take on new challenges, and pursue professional growth and career advancement.

jobs.title: Software Engineer
jobs.description:

• Proficient in Python, C, C++, or similar interpreted or low-level programming languages

Through this strategic partnership, we combine complementary expertise and capabilities to advance innovative immunotherapies for patients living with multiple myeloma.

Legend Biotech is seeking an Information Security Operations Analyst as part of the Information Technology team based in Somerset, NJ.

Role Overview

The Information Security Operations Analyst is a key member of the Information Security Office, responsible for operating, tuning, and monitoring the company’s security technology stack. The Analyst detects, triages, contains, and reports on security events; manages vulnerability, email, endpoint, network, and identity security controls; delivers the phishing simulation and awareness program; and produces operational security metrics in alignment with security frameworks and regulatory requirements.

Key Responsibilities

• Security monitoring & response: Monitor SIEM and alerting platforms; triage, investigate, and escalate alerts; support incident investigations, root cause analysis, and incident reporting.

• Detection tuning & platform health: Tune detection rules, risk scoring, and log sources; maintain collectors, integrations, certificates, and upgrades with vendors and Infrastructure.

• Vulnerability management: Run on-demand and scheduled scans for new servers, software, and changes; report results and track remediation with asset owners.

• Email security: Administer the secure email gateway, including quarantine, sender and policy rules, threat alert triage, and email DLP tuning.

• Identity threat response: Investigate risky sign-ins and suspicious MFA/device registrations; perform containment (session revocation, MFA reset, device removal).

• Endpoint, network & cloud security: Support EDR/XDR, MDM/UEM, secure web gateway, and ZTNA operations, including compliance reviews and policy rollouts.

• Security awareness: Design, run, and report on phishing simulations; align content with awareness events and support end-user training.

• Access & third-party risk: Remove privileged and security-tool access during offboarding; identify unapproved software and route requests through TPRM.

• Documentation & reporting: Maintain SOPs, KB articles, runbooks, monthly operations reports, and leadership metrics.

• Projects, audit & improvement: Support vendor POCs, new security implementations, internal/external audits, annual IT risk assessments, and program enhancements.

• Decision Making: Independently triages alerts, determines escalation to the Incident Response Manager, and executes first-line containment within established procedures. Recommends tuning, policy changes, and remediation priorities to the Global Manager, Network Security Operations; broader-impact changes follow change management.

Requirements

• Baccalaureate Degree or Post-graduate from an accredited university in Computer Science, Engineering or related field of study.

• Related certificates in Information Security.

• Five plus years’ experience in cybersecurity, utilizing security tools and cloud environment experience

• Experience with implementing and configuring security tools

• Experience with testing and evaluating security products

• Hands-on SOC experience, including alert triage, investigation, and incident response support

• Working knowledge of IT-related and compliance mandates (e.g. Sarbanes Oxley, HIPAA, GDPR, CCPA, PCI DSS, FDA) is desired

• Working knowledge of security frameworks and standards (NIST, ISO, CIS, COBIT)

• Excellent analytical and technical skills

• Professional planning and organizational skills, including presentation and strong written communication

• Ability to communicate technical information in understandable business terms

• Great interpersonal skills, including teamwork, facilitation and negotiating skills

• Ability to positively influence the behavior of peers and build relationships with other teams without direct authority over those teams

• Security operations: SIEM, vulnerability scanning, secure email gateway, EDR/XDR, MDM/UEM

• Network & identity: SWG/ZTNA, directory and cloud identity, SSO, SAML, MFA, conditional access, PAM/PIM

• Other: DLP concepts, ITSM ticketing; scripting (e.g., PowerShell) a plus
