Your Role at Baxter

This is where my hands make life-sustaining products

You are driven by the knowledge that the products you help make saves and sustain lives. You can move quickly, address questions, and encourage teammates, all while getting quality products out on time. You are calm, positive, and a key part of a fast-paced environment that emphasizes camaraderie and teamwork. As a Production Technician II, Kiefel, you are happiest when you are moving, and we will not disappoint!

Baxter is known for its speed and high-quality product. Our manufacturing operations are around-the-clock to meet the needs of our customers. Our high-caliber talent works through the challenges at hand while pushing toward meeting client order needs. Different shift assignments allow for flexibility and safety.

Watch this video to understand the garbing process (your required attire on the job) and what it means for patient safety.

Your team

Baxter is focused on saving and sustaining lives by manufacturing high-quality products. We strive to create quality products for our customers each day.

Delivering life-saving products is about getting them right, and attention to detail is how we make sure we meet that challenge. We are a team that supports each other throughout each shift. Working together in a supportive and open culture makes our processes evolve for the better and engages our workforce.

You'll be offered extensive training, and the tight-knit working environment within the Manufacturing team means employees get additional training from their direct manager and peers when needed.

What we offer from Day One:

• Shift flexibility to trade shifts and leverage overtime opportunities
• Medical, Dental and Vision coverage
• 160 hours of Paid Time Off and Paid Holidays
• 401K match
• Employee Stock Purchase Program
• Paid Parental Leave
• Tuition Reimbursement

What You'll Be Doing

The Kiefel Production Technician II is a Salary Non-Exempt position which contributes to our mission of saving and sustaining lives by supplying, operating and maintaining a set of Kiefel Machines in addition to inspecting and performing quality checks on the finished bags as necessary. Kiefel Production Technician will be the primary resource for identifying and correcting any maintenance issues on the Kiefel.

• Act as a SME in machine operations and Kiefel processes.
• Perform routine and preventative maintenance such as alignment adjustments, replacement of machine parts or belts, cleaning and lubrication while supporting Total Productive Maintenance (TPM).
• Investigate, identify and correct or escalate any inefficiency in the machine’s performance.
• Conduct on-the-job training for Kiefel Production Technicians.
• Document completed maintenance activity and follow up work orders in Maximo.
• Load and secure finished product in mobile closets as well as scan containers in to GME (inventory system)
• Execute a machine changeover (including main seal die) when necessary. Certification must be received to complete associated task.
• Test, inspect and package Inter-Plant Shipping Orders (IPSO).
• Perform and document scheduled cleaning activities.
• Notify the supervisor and take appropriate action if any safety, quality, mechanical or discrepancy issues occur.
• Take a leadership role in sustaining a clean and safe work area using 6S principles including maintaining and securing provided tools
• Participate on teams that help generate ideas in process improvements to equipment.
• Learn, understand and apply rigorous quality standards, Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and Current Good Manufacturing Practices (cGMP).

What You'll Bring

• Must have basic English written and oral communication skills adequate to communicate with other team members.
• Understand verbal and written safety and quality instructions and read and comprehend written work instructions including words and drawings.
• Must be able to perform basic mathematics.
• Will need to be able to understand the complex mechanical and electrical aspects of the Kiefel machine in order to maintain and make the necessary repairs.
• Proficient in how to use measurement tools (Caliper, Microscope, Micrometer, Ruler, Taper Gauge, etc.) as well as basic hand tools.
• Basic computer skills
• High School Diploma, GED or equivalent.
• Must be at least 18 years of age.
• 2-3 years of Production Technician or manufacturing experience with duties including preventative maintenance, machine troubleshooting, etc.

Physical Requirements

• The ability to push/pull and lift/carry up to 50 pounds and stand/walk continuously throughout the shift.
• Pass the P.I.V. physical.
• Normal visual acuity.
• Ability to squat, climb, reach above shoulder level, reach at or below shoulder level, kneel, twist and bend at the neck, twist and bend at the waist and balance.

Responsible for leading and strategic planning of the North Cove Controls Engineering organization. Provides coaching and mentorship to the North Cove Controls Engineering function and is accountable for the site’s performance and key initiatives related to upgrading and improving equipment performance as it pertains to controls. Responsible for the area budget and headcount resources. Directs the team to complete projects and programs within boundaries of quality, time, and budget.

Based on significant technical and managerial expertise, creates and implements strategies that improve Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE), equipment performance, process capability, automation reliability, and manufacturing productivity across the site’s various manufacturing cells. Provides technical direction to staff and fosters an environment of creativity, innovation, collaboration, and continuous improvement in achieving departmental and site objectives. • Strong understanding of PLCs, HMIs, SCADA systems, industrial networks, motion control systems, robotics, machine vision systems, data analytics platforms, and manufacturing control architectures.
• Proven track record of management and leadership effectiveness in manufacturing and engineering environments.
• Strong project management and capital planning capabilities with demonstrated success executing complex, multi-site engineering initiatives.

jobs.title: Material Handler, Cell Therapy
jobs.description:
At Bristol Myers Squibb, our employees often ask, “Who are you working for?”—a question that fuels collaboration, accountability, and urgency in our work. Our purpose-driven culture inspires us to discover, develop, and deliver innovative medicines to prevail over serious diseases. We offer uniquely interesting and meaningful work, opportunities for growth, and a supportive environment that values inclusion, wellbeing, flexibility, and comprehensive benefits. This is work that transforms the lives of patients, and the careers of those who do it.

At Bristol Myers Squibb we are reimagining the future of cell therapy. With our bold ambition, backed by a best-in-the-industry team and long-term commitment, we are leading the way to unlock the full promise of cell therapy as we strive to put more patients on the path to a cure. If you are ready to challenge yourself, accelerate your career, and give new hope to patients, there’s no better place than here at BMS with our Cell Therapy team.

The Material Handler role is responsible to perform routine Material Operations in the receiving dock, warehouse, and controlled temperature locations within the multiproduct Cell Therapy Facility to support the production of commercial and clinical products.

Shifts Available:

Monday – Friday, 8am – 4pm, onsite

Responsibilities will include, but are not limited to the following:

• Operate with safety, quality, and integrity as core principles
• Perform goods receipt of SAP managed consumables and raw materials on receiving dock
• Put materials away into SAP managed bin locations within warehouse and other controlled temperature locations
• Execute inventory cycle counts
• Perform material replenishment to the Kitting Department and other customers within the facility
• This is an operations role where ~90% of time is spent on the floor executing the job functions
• Perform material picking and putaway at heights of up to 25 feet using Powered Industrial Truck
• Operate Powered Industrial Trucks including forklifts and Turret Trucks for material movement in a safe and efficient manner
• Operate pallet wrapper in a safe and efficient manner
• Understand and follow CGMP practices in accordance with effective controlled documentation (i.e. SOP, Work Practice)
• Collaborate and partner with stakeholder groups such as Incoming QA, Planning, and Quality Control
• Complete CGMP paperwork using GDocP principles
• Cross-train into Kitting Department to build material kits to support production
• Cross-train into Product Services to assist with final Drug Product pack-out operations

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities:

• Microsoft Office Applications such as Outlook, PowerPoint, Excel, and Word
• Ability to work independently and as part of a team
• ERP system knowledge and experience (SAP is preferred)
• Experience with domestic and international shipping (GMP raw materials and consumables is preferred)
• Experience in a commercial biotech environment is preferred
• Cold chain material receipt and handling
• Experience with pallet wrapper, forklift, and turret truck is preferred
• Experience and familiarity with the Quality Management System and documentation of change control, deviations, and CAPA is preferred
• Ability to lift up to 50 pounds and regularly bend, reach and walk

Minimum Requirements:

• High school Diploma / GED. Additional post-secondary education resulting in an Associate’s or Bachelor’s Degree in a relevant discipline is preferred
• An equivalent combination of education, experience and training may substitute
• Preferred but not required: Certification in CPIM, CSCP, and/or CLTD

BMSCART

#LI-ONSITE

We hire for skills and capabilities, not just credentials – if this role excites you, but doesn’t perfectly match your resume, we encourage you to apply anyway.

Devens - MA - US: $30.81 - $37.33per hour

jobs.title: VP, Engineering
jobs.description:
Since 1869, we've connected people through food they love. We’re proud to be stewards of amazing brands that people trust. Our portfolio includes the iconic Campbell’s brand, as well as Cape Cod, Chunky, Goldfish, Kettle Brand, Lance, Late July, Pacific Foods, Pepperidge Farm, Prego, Pace, Rao’s Homemade, Snack Factory, Snyder’s of Hanover. Swanson, and V8.

Here, you will make a difference every day. You will be supported to build a rewarding career with opportunities to grow, innovate and inspire. Make history with us.

Why Campbell’s…

• Benefits begin on day one and include medical, dental, short and long-term disability, AD&D, and life insurance (for individual, families, and domestic partners).
• Employees are eligible for our matching 401(k) plan and can enroll on the first day of employment with immediate vesting.
• Campbell’s offers unlimited sick time along with paid time off and holiday pay.
• If in WHQ – free access to the fitness center. Access to on-site day care (operated by Bright Horizons) and company store.
• Giving back to the communities where our employees work and live is very important to Campbell’s. Our “Campbell’s Cares” program matches employee donations and/or volunteer activity up to $1,500 annually.
• Campbell’s has a variety of Employee Resource Groups (ERGs) to support employees.

Position Summary

The Vice President of Engineering provides enterprise leadership for engineering strategy, capital investment, automation, infrastructure, manufacturing technology, and technical capability across the manufacturing network. This executive is accountable for translating business priorities into safe, reliable, scalable, and financially sound solutions that strengthen growth, productivity, innovation, sustainability, quality, and operational performance.

The VP of Engineering leads through partnership and service. This leader brings together Manufacturing, Operations, Supply Chain, R&D, Quality, Finance, Procurement, EH&S, Human Resources, Commercial, and external experts to define needs, evaluate alternatives, and deliver the best enterprise outcome. The role creates clarity, removes barriers, develops people, and enables teams closest to the work to contribute meaningfully to solution design and execution.

The role oversees an annual capital portfolio exceeding $150 million and ensures that the strongest available internal and external expertise is applied to major capital programs, network investments, technology modernization, and complex operational challenges. Success requires disciplined governance, shared ownership, rigorous technical review, and solutions that are practical to operate, maintain, and sustain.

Key Responsibilities

Engineering Strategy, Servant Leadership & Capability

•	Develop and execute a multi-year enterprise engineering strategy aligned with business growth, network needs, productivity, sustainability, innovation, and operational excellence priorities.

•	Lead with a servant leadership mindset by listening actively, creating clarity, removing organizational and technical barriers, and enabling teams to perform at their best.

•	Build a high-performing, inclusive engineering organization that values humility, accountability, curiosity, collaboration, and service to manufacturing and the broader enterprise.

•	Develop engineering talent through coaching, stretch assignments, succession planning, communities of practice, and purposeful exposure to enterprise priorities.

•	Establish clear engineering standards, governance, project management disciplines, and decision rights while empowering capable teams to act with appropriate speed and ownership.

•	Create an environment where technical debate is welcomed, lessons are shared, and the best idea is advanced regardless of its source.

Cross-Functional Solution Development

•	Partner with Manufacturing, Operations, Supply Chain, R&D, Quality, Finance, Procurement, EH&S, HR, Commercial, and other stakeholders from problem definition through design, execution, commissioning, and benefits realization.

•	Ensure business, operational, technical, safety, quality, financial, workforce, and customer perspectives are integrated into major decisions and solution designs.

•	Build shared ownership by engaging plant teams, operators, maintenance, technical specialists, and functional leaders early and throughout the project lifecycle.

•	Facilitate alignment across stakeholders, surface tradeoffs transparently, and resolve issues in the best interest of the enterprise rather than a single function.

•	Partner with innovation and commercial teams to ensure new products, processes, and technologies are designed for manufacturability, scalability, reliability, and sustainable execution.

•	Use influence, trust, and fact-based recommendations to align senior leaders around complex enterprise decisions.

Technical Excellence & Expertise Networks

•	Establish a deliberate approach for identifying, convening, and leveraging the best available internal and external expertise for each opportunity or challenge.

•	Create strong technical networks and communities of practice across processing, packaging, utilities, facilities, automation, controls, reliability, digital manufacturing, and project execution.

•	Ensure major solutions receive rigorous multidisciplinary technical review, appropriate challenge, and validation before investment and implementation.

•	Engage subject matter experts, manufacturing teams, strategic suppliers, consultants, and industry partners based on the needs and risks of the work.

•	Promote standardization and reuse of proven designs while allowing thoughtful adaptation to site, product, process, and customer requirements.

•	Capture and share technical knowledge, project learnings, benchmarks, and standards so expertise is scalable across the network and not concentrated in individuals or locations.

•	Benchmark external practices and emerging technologies to maintain best-in-class technical capability and avoid insular decision-making.

Capital Portfolio Management & Project Delivery

•	Lead and govern an annual capital investment portfolio of $150M+ in partnership with business, finance, manufacturing, supply chain, and functional leaders.

•	Develop long-range capital plans that support capacity, network optimization, automation, infrastructure renewal, asset reliability, compliance, growth, and cost competitiveness.

•	Prioritize investments using transparent criteria that consider strategic value, operational need, technical risk, financial return, resource capacity, and enterprise interdependencies.

•	Ensure project teams apply fit-for-purpose governance, front-end planning, risk management, technical assurance, change control, and benefits tracking.

•	Create shared accountability for projects to be delivered safely, on time, within budget, and with the intended operational and financial outcomes.

•	Ensure solutions are developed with the people who will operate and maintain them, with clear plans for training, commissioning, startup, handoff, and sustained performance.

Manufacturing & Operational Excellence

•	Partner with manufacturing and plant leadership to improve safety, asset utilization, throughput, reliability, quality, yield, labor effectiveness, and cost performance.

•	Apply Lean, TPM, Six Sigma, reliability-centered maintenance, and other relevant methodologies in ways that build local capability and solve the underlying business need.

•	Champion practical digital manufacturing, automation, controls, data, and smart factory solutions that strengthen decision-making and workforce effectiveness.

•	Provide responsive technical support for complex operating challenges while building the capability of teams to diagnose, solve, and prevent recurrence.

•	Balance near-term operational support with long-term asset, technology, and capability strategies.

Safety, Quality, Compliance & Sustainability

•	Embed worker safety, food safety, quality, environmental stewardship, cybersecurity, and regulatory compliance into the earliest stages of engineering decisions and designs.

•	Ensure engineering standards and solutions meet applicable corporate, FDA, OSHA, environmental, and industry requirements.

•	Partner with EH&S, Quality, Operations, and technical experts to identify risk, apply appropriate controls, and verify that solutions perform as intended.

•	Advance sustainability priorities, including energy efficiency, waste reduction, water conservation, emissions reduction, and responsible use of resources.

Innovation & Technology Advancement

•	Evaluate emerging technologies and industry practices through structured collaboration with

R&D, Operations, IT, Supply Chain, Procurement, suppliers, and technical partners.

•	Lead disciplined pilots and scale-up efforts that test technical feasibility, operational value, workforce impact, and economic return before broader deployment.

•	Enable innovative processing, packaging, automation, digital, and infrastructure solutions that improve growth, resilience, productivity, quality, and cost competitiveness.

•	Ensure technology decisions are interoperable, supportable, secure, and aligned with enterprise architecture and long-term manufacturing strategy.

Qualifications

Required

•	Bachelor's degree in Engineering, including Mechanical, Chemical, Electrical, Industrial, or a related discipline.

•	Minimum 15 years of progressive engineering leadership experience within food, beverage, consumer packaged goods, or a related manufacturing industry.

•	Minimum 10 years leading large, multi-site engineering organizations or complex enterprise technical networks.

•	Demonstrated accountability for an annual capital portfolio exceeding $150 million.

•	Proven success delivering large-scale capital programs, automation initiatives, infrastructure projects, and manufacturing transformations through cross-functional teams.

•	Demonstrated ability to mobilize diverse expertise, make sound technical decisions, and convert complex business needs into sustainable solutions.

•	Experience developing engineering talent, building organizational capability, and leading through influence across a geographically dispersed network.

Preferred

•	Master's degree in Engineering, Business Administration, or a related field.

•	Professional Engineer (PE) certification.

•	Lean, TPM, Six Sigma, project management, or reliability certification.

Critical Leadership Competencies

•	Servant Leadership and Team Enablement

•	Cross-Functional Collaboration and Enterprise Partnership

•	Technical Stewardship and Expert Network Leadership

•	Strategic and Enterprise Thinking

•	Capital Portfolio and Financial Acumen

•	Manufacturing and Operational Excellence

•	Influence, Alignment, and Stakeholder Management

•	Talent Development and Succession Planning

•	Change Leadership and Organizational Transformation

•	Innovation, Curiosity, and External Orientation

•	Judgment, Accountability, and Risk Management

•	Learning Agility and Knowledge Sharing

Success Profile

The ideal candidate is a collaborative executive who combines deep technical credibility with strong business judgment and a genuine commitment to serving teams and the enterprise. This leader does not assume that the engineering function alone has the answer. Instead, they ask the right questions, engage the people closest to the work, connect the organization to the strongest available expertise, and create the conditions for teams to develop and execute superior solutions.

They are recognized for building trust across functions, developing talent, raising technical standards, and delivering complex programs through shared ownership and disciplined execution. They balance enterprise consistency with local insight, challenge assumptions constructively, and ensure decisions reflect safety, quality, operational, financial, workforce, and customer needs. They translate long-term strategy into practical action while strengthening capability across a large, geographically dispersed manufacturing network.

Key Experience Requirements

•	Led engineering for a multi-site food, beverage, consumer packaged goods, or comparable manufacturing network.

•	Managed annual capital investments of $150M+ with disciplined governance and demonstrated business outcomes.

•	Directed major automation, digital manufacturing, processing, packaging, utilities, facilities, or infrastructure programs.

•	Built effective partnerships across Manufacturing, Operations, R&D, Supply Chain, Finance, Procurement, Quality, EH&S, HR, IT, and Commercial functions.

jobs.description:
Since 1869, we've connected people through food they love. We’re proud to be stewards of amazing brands that people trust. Our portfolio includes the iconic Campbell’s brand, as well as Cape Cod, Chunky, Goldfish, Kettle Brand, Lance, Late July, Pacific Foods, Pepperidge Farm, Prego, Pace, Rao’s Homemade, Snack Factory, Snyder’s of Hanover. Swanson, and V8.

Here, you will make a difference every day. You will be supported to build a rewarding career with opportunities to grow, innovate and inspire. Make history with us.

Packaging Machine Operator

Location: Hanover, Pennsylvania

Shift: 1st Shift | 7:00 AM - 3:00 PM Monday - Friday

Starting Pay: $25.50/hour

HOW YOU WILL MAKE HISTORY HERE…

As a Packaging Machine Operator, you will play a critical role in delivering high-quality products to our customers by safely and efficiently operating packaging equipment. Your attention to quality, troubleshooting expertise, and commitment to continuous improvement help ensure products are packaged accurately while maintaining production efficiency and food safety standards.

WHAT YOU WILL DO…

• Maintain shift documentation, including metal detector checks and batch order verifications.
• Read and interpret production schedules using MicroStrategy.
• Print labels using various printers and programs; clean and adjust printers as needed.
• Perform nitrogen testing and other quality checks.
• Monitor packaging machinery to ensure correct codes, dates, and pricing information.
• Maintain adequate supplies of roll stock and packaging materials.
• Set up and program bag-making equipment.
• Create and edit machine settings and micro logic to support efficient, low-waste operations.
• Create and modify code dates.
• Perform preventative maintenance, minor repairs, and equipment adjustments.
• Calibrate and adjust scales, linkages, and packaging equipment components.
• Operate packaging equipment, including baggers, scales, conveyors, seal checkers, case packers, case sealers, and robotic cells.
• Plan and execute efficient machine changeovers between product runs.
• Monitor and adjust machines to ensure proper film cut-off and seal quality.
• Ensure machines are operating at established production standards and speeds.
• Monitor product appearance and comply with weight control requirements.
• Perform bag weight checks every 20 minutes and inspect products for quality concerns.
• Identify, troubleshoot, and resolve packaging quality issues.
• Sort and rework acceptable product from run-off as required.
• Maintain clean machines and work areas through routine sanitation and housekeeping.
• Report equipment issues promptly to maintenance technicians or supervisors.
• Follow all safety, food safety, hygiene, and housekeeping procedures.
• Store supplies in designated locations and keep aisles and exits clear.
• May provide leadership and direction to Packers.
• May serve as a Back-Up Packaging Coordinator or other skilled production roles.
• May monitor and replenish seasoning systems to ensure proper product coverage.
• Perform other duties as assigned.
• Work overtime as required to support production needs.

WHO YOU WILL WORK WITH…

• Packers
• Packaging Coordinators
• Maintenance Technicians
• Production Supervisors
• Quality and Food Safety Teams
• Sanitation Team Members
• Warehouse and Logistics Teams
• Manufacturing Support Teams

WHAT YOU BRING TO THE TABLE… (MUST HAVE)

• Strong mechanical aptitude and troubleshooting skills.
• Ability to safely operate manufacturing and packaging equipment.
• Ability to perform machine setups, changeovers, adjustments, and basic maintenance activities.
• Strong attention to detail with a focus on product quality and food safety.
• Ability to work in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.
• Ability to follow written procedures, production schedules, and safety guidelines.
• Ability to lift, carry, push, pull, bend, twist, and stand for extended periods.
• Willingness to work overtime during the week and on weekends based on production requirements.
• Commitment to teamwork, safety, and continuous improvement.

IT WOULD BE GREAT IF YOU HAVE… (NICE TO HAVE)

• High School Diploma or GED.
• One (1) year of production experience in a manufacturing environment.
• Previous experience operating packaging equipment in a food manufacturing environment.
• Experience with automated equipment, robotic cells, or case packing equipment.
• Knowledge of MicroStrategy or other production management systems.
• Experience with preventative maintenance and equipment troubleshooting.
• Leadership experience in a manufacturing environment.

Physical & Work Environment

• Continuous standing, hand use, visual focus, and fine motor movements throughout the shift.
• Frequent walking, bending, reaching, carrying, pushing, pulling, overhead work, squatting, kneeling, and climbing activities.
• Continuous repetitive twisting and manual manipulation of equipment and packaging materials.
• Frequent reading, writing, concentration, comprehension, and problem-solving while monitoring equipment and product quality.
• Ability to lift up to 10 pounds continuously, up to 25 pounds frequently, and up to 50 pounds frequently.
• Ability to lift up to 100 pounds occasionally with assistance and over 100 pounds seldom with assistance.
• Regular exposure to moving mechanical equipment and manufacturing machinery.
• Frequent exposure to wet and humid production environments.
• Occasional exposure to elevated work areas, airborne particles, and cleaning chemicals.
• Work is performed in a loud manufacturing environment requiring appropriate Personal Protective Equipment (PPE).
• Fast-paced production environment focused on safety, quality, efficiency, and continuous improvement.

GENERAL FUNCTION:

The Fraud Analyst I is a cross functional position within Fraud Operations. Fraud Analyst Is can support the Fraud Detection, Fraud Communication, and Domestic Collections teams based on staffing and business needs.

Fraud Detection - Responsible for analyzing and decisioning alerts on fraud detection systems to determine what actions need to be taken (e.g., placing holds, opening cases, etc.). Fraud Detection responsibilities includes both verbal and written communication to internal and external customers.

Fraud Communication – Responsible for handling direct communications with bank customers, bank employees, and offshore fraud call service partners. Communications are handled via phone calls (customer, bank employees, offshore partner) and chat (Retail bank employees and offshore partner).

Domestic Collections – Responsible for processing and decisioning fraud check dispute claims. Includes working alerts, dispute cases and inbound call inquiries supporting the customer, retail partner and bank transfers.

Fraud Detection, Fraud Communication, and Domestic Collections functions require attention to detail, multi-tasking, communication, and critical thinking skills. Fraud Analyst Is also assist Fraud Operations leadership in developing policies and procedures to enhance processes and reduce fraud risk.

Responsible and accountable for risk by openly exchanging ideas and opinions, elevating concerns, and personally following policies and procedures as defined. Accountable for always doing the right thing for customers and colleagues and ensures that actions and behaviors drive a positive customer experience. While operating within the Banks risk appetite, achieves results by consistently identifying, assessing, managing, monitoring, and reporting risks of all types.

About the role

As a member of the Vulnerability Management and Patching team, you will help strengthen the organization’s security posture by identifying vulnerabilities, prioritizing remediation, and supporting effective patch management across the technology environment. The role involves working closely with system owners and application teams to drive timely remediation while maintaining visibility into vulnerability, patching, and compliance status.

Your key responsibilities

• Perform regular vulnerability scans using tools such as Qualys, Tenable, or Rapid7.
• Analyze vulnerability scan results and prioritize vulnerabilities based on risk.
• Coordinate remediation and mitigation activities with system owners and application teams.
• Track vulnerability remediation progress, metrics, and compliance status.
• Maintain vulnerability management documentation, processes, and procedures.
• Administer and maintain IBM BigFix infrastructure for patch deployment and compliance reporting.
• Develop and test custom Fixlets, baselines, and automation scripts.
• Schedule and deploy operating system and third-party patches across Windows, Linux, and macOS environments.
• Support vulnerability remediation across Windows and Linux server environments.
• Monitor patch deployment successes and failures and troubleshoot deployment issues.
• Generate compliance reports and dashboards to support internal reporting and audit requirements.

What you bring

• Hands-on experience with vulnerability scanning and management using Qualys, Tenable, Rapid7, or similar tools.
• Experience administering IBM BigFix and managing enterprise patch deployments.
• Practical knowledge of vulnerability remediation for Windows and Linux servers.
• Experience deploying operating system and third-party patches across Windows, Linux, and/or macOS environments.
• Ability to analyze vulnerability findings, understand risk and prioritize remediation activities.
• Strong troubleshooting and problem-solving skills.
• Ability to work collaboratively with infrastructure, application, and system-owner teams.

• Experience developing and maintaining IBM BigFix Fixlets and baselines.
• Experience creating automation scripts to support patching or vulnerability remediation activities.

In this role, you will contribute directly to reducing security exposure by helping teams identify, prioritize, and remediate vulnerabilities across the technology environment. Client Success Associate – New Client Engagement

Hiring near our Fort Myers, FL Center of Excellence

What makes Gartner a great place to work?

We're recognized worldwide as a great place to work year after year. We've been recognized by Fortune as one of the World’s Most Admired Companies, named a Best Place to Work for LGBTQ Equality by the Human Rights Campaign Corporate Equality Index and a Best Place to Work for Disability Inclusion by the Disability Equality Index. Our teams are composed of individuals from different geographies, cultures, religions, ethnicities, races, genders, sexual orientations, abilities and generations. In our collaborative and supportive culture, you’ll make deep connections with colleagues, clients and the communities in which we live and work. You'll have the autonomy to get your work done with the flexibility you need to achieve your best.

About the role:

The Client Success team follows a Client for Life Philosophy, and individuals in this role ensure that every Gartner client receives value far exceeding their investment. Associates seek to understand and surface client’s business priorities, breakdown challenges, and identify the most effective ways to support the client in making the right decisions for their business. They are responsible for articulating Gartner value to prospective clients, onboarding clients, proving the concept of Gartner services, and stimulating client engagement of products.

New Client Engagement (NCE), a part of our Client Success Organization, is a fast-paced, dynamic business unit focused on providing the highest level of service to prospects and clients. NCE is made up of two functions: Client Onboarding and Insights Platform Walkthrough for prospects.

The Client Onboarding role focuses on providing a customized experience for new and upgraded clients. The Insights Platform Walkthrough team provides pre-sale demonstrations of Gartner resources, including our gartner.com platform, to prospects as a part of the sales process.

The NCE team utilizes Gartner assets, coupled with our gartner.com platform, to provide a valuable client experience that starts with a prospect demonstration by an NCE Insights Platform Walkthrough specialist, moves to an extensive client onboarding experience by an NCE Client Onboarding Specialist and transitions seamlessly to a service delivery associate for ongoing support.

You’ll apply strategic thinking and relationship building to help executives solve their most pressing business challenges. You will understand their critical initiatives, align Gartner research and expertise, and help contribute to Gartner’s growth.

What you will do:

• Lead prospect and/or client calls to understand client priorities and challenges and articulate the value of Gartner’s renowned products and services. Understand and communicate Gartner services and capabilities to prospective clients and demonstrate value to decision makers.

• Collaborate with our Sales teams on how to effectively demonstrate Gartner products and resources to prospects or clients to increase likelihood of engaging and purchasing a license. Communicate with internal Gartner partners to overcome obstacles and maximize the value Gartner delivers to prospects and clients.

• Research prospective and existing companies, C-Level executives, business trends, and competitive intelligence to prepare relevant and tailored Gartner resources to drive impact.

What you will need:

• Bachelor’s degree preferred

• 6+ months relevant professional and/or internship experience with a proven track record of success fueled by a passion for driving client success.

• Ability to demonstrate strong communication, collaboration, prioritization, critical thinking, and influencing skills; ability to be agile and flexible

• Well defined time management and organizational skills

What you will get:

• Competitive salary, generous paid time off policy, charity match program, Medical, Dental & Vision Plans, Parental Leave, Employee Assistance Program (EAP), 401K matching and more!

• Collaborative, team-oriented culture that embraces diversity

• Professional development and unlimited growth opportunities

• World-class training through our Academy when you join and on-going training from our L&D team and leadership

Who are we?

At Gartner, Inc. (NYSE:IT), we guide the leaders who shape the world.

Our mission relies on expert analysis and bold ideas to deliver actionable, objective business and technology insights, helping enterprise leaders and their teams succeed with their mission-critical priorities.

Since our founding in 1979, we’ve grown to 20,000 associates globally who support over 13,000 client enterprises in ~90 countries and territories. We do important, interesting and substantive work that matters. That’s why we hire associates with the intellectual curiosity, energy and drive to want to make a difference. The bar is unapologetically high. So is the impact you can have here.

What makes Gartner a great place to work?

Our vast, virtually untapped market potential offers limitless opportunities – opportunities that may not even exist right now – for you to grow professionally and flourish personally. How far you go is driven by your passion and performance.

We hire remarkable people who collaborate and win as a team. Together, our singular, unifying goal is to deliver results for our clients.

Our teams are inclusive and composed of individuals from different geographies, cultures, religions, ethnicities, races, genders, sexual orientations, abilities and generations.

We invest in great leaders who bring out the best in you and the company, enabling us to multiply our impact and results. This is why, year after year, we are recognized worldwide as a great place to work.

Gartner is the world authority on AI

At Gartner, you’ll join a company at the very center of the AI revolution. Gartner has proactive, objective guidance throughout clients’ AI journeys. We set the standard for how organizations leverage artificial intelligence to drive meaningful impact. You’ll have access to unmatched resources, expertise, and technology, and play a key role in helping Gartner and our clients innovate and grow as we leverage AI to transform business and technology landscapes.

It’s an exciting time to be at Gartner, with limitless opportunities to make a real impact, grow your skills, and build a lasting, meaningful career in a field that’s reshaping the way we operate. If you’re passionate about AI and want to be part of a team that’s guiding the leaders who shape the world, Gartner is the place for you.

What do we offer?

Gartner offers world-class benefits, highly competitive compensation and disproportionate rewards for top performers.

In our hybrid work environment, we provide the flexibility and support for you to thrive — working virtually when it's productive to do so and getting together with colleagues in a vibrant community that is purposeful, engaging and inspiring.

Ready to grow your career with Gartner? Join us.

Gartner believes in fair and equitable pay. A reasonable estimate of the base salary range for this role is 53,000 USD - 77,000 USD. Please note that actual salaries may vary within the range, or be above or below the range, based on factors including, but not limited to, education, training, experience, professional achievement, business need, and location. In addition to base salary, employees will participate in either an annual bonus plan based on company and individual performance, or a role-based, uncapped sales incentive plan. Job Description:

Senior Principal Solution Test & Automation Engineer - Customer Engagement

Location (HYBRID):  Sunnyvale, CA

HPE Networking is seeking a Senior Principal Solution Test & Automation Engineer to lead quality engineering for large-scale networking and distributed software solutions. This is a highly technical Individual Contributor role requiring substantial technical impact on strategic products, architectural initiatives, and customer success. The role combines deep software testing expertise, system-level engineering knowledge, customer engagement, and technical leadership. The successful candidate will serve as a go-to authority for complex quality engineering challenges, drive innovation in automation and validation, and influence product quality, scalability, observability, and reliability across the entire product lifecycle.

You will partner closely with engineering, architecture, product management, sales engineering, services, support, and customers to validate complex networking solutions, establish scalable quality engineering practices, and deliver long-lasting improvements to engineering productivity and product quality. In addition to technical execution, you will provide leadership across functions, mentor engineers, and help define the future direction of solution validation and automation.

Success in this role requires substantial technical impact on significant products and programs, recognized expertise within the organization, leadership across functions, delivery of long-lasting test engineering improvements, mentorship of technical talent, and innovation that advances customer outcomes and business objectives.

Solution Validation & Customer Engagement

• Understand customer deployments, business requirements, architectures, and large-scale operational environments to develop comprehensive validation strategies.
• Lead validation efforts for strategic customer solutions and complex networking deployments.
• Collaborate with customers, field engineers, solution architects, sales engineers, and services teams to validate real-world networking solutions and operational readiness.
• Participate in and influence technical design workshops, architecture reviews, and strategic planning discussions to improve reliability, scalability, observability, and serviceability.
• Translate customer requirements into repeatable, solution-focused validation frameworks.
• Present technical findings, risk assessments, quality recommendations, and executive-level updates to customers and internal stakeholders.
• Drive cross-functional initiatives that improve customer outcomes and product quality.

Automation & Quality Engineering

• Define and drive automation strategy across products, programs, and engineering teams.
• Architect, develop, and evolve scalable automation frameworks supporting functional, integration, system, resiliency, scale, performance, and solution validation.
• Establish engineering best practices and standards for continuous validation through CI/CD pipelines.
• Lead innovation in automation infrastructure, tooling, and AI-assisted engineering practices.
• Drive organization-wide adoption of quality engineering methodologies that improve time-to-market and engineering productivity.
• Identify opportunities to simplify validation workflows and reduce operational costs through automation.

System-Level Testing & Debugging

• Lead validation of distributed, multi-component software and networking platforms at scale.
• Execute and automate regression, longevity, fault-injection, recovery, scalability, interoperability, and performance testing.
• Utilize logs, metrics, traces, telemetry, observability platforms, and diagnostic frameworks to troubleshoot complex failures.
• Lead root-cause investigations spanning multiple teams and technology domains.
• Differentiate product defects from infrastructure, automation, and environmental issues.
• Influence architecture and design decisions to improve product testability, diagnosability, and operational excellence.

Technical Leadership

• Provide technical leadership for strategic initiatives, major releases, and architectural programs.
• Serve as a recognized authority for solution validation, automation, and quality engineering.
• Lead and connect engineering teams across functions to align around common quality objectives.
• Drive quality-first engineering practices throughout the development lifecycle.
• Mentor engineers through technical guidance, reviews, coaching, and knowledge sharing.
• Contribute to technical innovation through patents, white papers, standards participation, publications, and architectural proposals.
• Build long-term technical capabilities that create recurring business value and customer impact.

Basic Qualifications

Software Engineering & Automation

• Expert-level programming expertise in Python, Go, or C++, with deep proficiency in at least one language.
• Extensive experience designing and building automation platforms, frameworks, and quality engineering ecosystems.
• Experience integrating large-scale automated testing into CI/CD environments.
• Proven history of driving transformational automation initiatives.

Systems & Networking

• Strong understanding of Linux/UNIX operating systems, networking, processes, memory management, and system internals.
• Extensive experience validating distributed and multi-component systems.
• Deep hands-on expertise configuring and validating multi-vendor networking environments.
• Experience supporting service provider, enterprise, and cloud networking deployments.
• Strong knowledge of performance testing and traffic-generation platforms such as Ixia and Spirent.

Testing & Quality Engineering

• Deep expertise in system-level and end-to-end validation.
• Multi-feature, longevity, resiliency, interoperability, scale, and performance testing.
• Fault injection and recovery validation.
• Root-cause analysis and complex defect investigation.
• Advanced troubleshooting across multiple software and infrastructure layers.

Leadership & Influence

• Demonstrated history of leading significant technical initiatives with measurable business impact.
• Proven ability to influence engineering decisions, architecture, and strategic direction.
• Experience mentoring engineers and leading cross-functional technical initiatives.

Preferred Qualifications

• Advanced networking expertise in Layer 2, Layer 3, TCP/IP, Routing, MPLS, EVPN, and data center technologies.
• Experience with network operating systems, cloud infrastructure, observability platforms, and distributed architectures.
• Working knowledge of JUNOS.
• Industry certifications such as JNCIE, CCIE, or equivalent.
• Experience leveraging AI-assisted engineering tools for automation development, test generation, diagnostics, failure analysis, and productivity improvements.
• Track record of innovation resulting in patents, publications, standards contributions, or architectural leadership.

Accessibility

HPE is committed to creating an inclusive and accessible workplace and encourages applications from all qualified individuals, including those with disabilities. If you believe you require accommodation during any stage of the application or interview process, please submit your request by completing our secure form linked here.

Note: This option is reserved for applicants needing assistance/reasonable accommodation related to a disability.

Personal & Professional Development

We also invest in your career because the better you are, the better we all are. We have specific programs catered to helping you reach any career goals you have — whether you want to become a knowledge expert in your field or apply your skills to another division.

Unconditional Inclusion

We are unconditionally inclusive in the way we work and celebrate individual uniqueness. We know varied backgrounds are valued and succeed here. We have the flexibility to manage our work and personal needs. We make bold moves, together, and are a force for good.
